item.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
item.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. item.title: 7 Years Later, Hollywood’s Most Notorious Fantasy Flop Deserves Another Shot
item.description: I vividly remember learning the phrase “uncanny valley” in 2019. First came the trailer for Sonic the Hedgehog that April, with those alarmingly human teeth. Then came the first trailer for Tom Hooper’s Cats in July. Suddenly, there was a name for a feeling I’d had my whole life. The uncanny valley is that uneasy feeling you get when something looks or moves almost like a real person, but some small detail makes the whole thing feel wrong. That feeling is a lot more common these days, now that AI-generated videos are everywhere. But it was Cats that really brought the uncanny valley into the popular lexicon.

item.title: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
item.description: The Forerunner 265S is great for runners with small wrists. | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it. Garmin Forerunner 265S (42mm) Garmin’s Forerunner 265S is identical to the standard 265, only it features a slightly better battery life and a smaller 42mm build for those with more petite wrists. Where to Buy: $449.99 $299.99 at Amazon $449.99 $299.99 at Best Buy The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds. There are a few other Garmin models I like that are also on sale during Black Friday. I wish that I had 10 arms to fully vet every single last one, but alas. That said, here are some others that I have tested and recommend: The Garmin Fenix 8 is $749 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , which is a 25 percent discount off its original price. Its higher price comes down to having more features than the Forerunner 265S, so it’s really best for someone who does multiple outdoor sports and could make use of its handy LED flashlight. Garmin’s Venu 4 is $449 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , an 18 percent discount. This is a great option if you’re looking for more of a smartwatch that does fitness than a fitness-y watch that looks like a smartwatch. It’s a fine line, but if you know, you know. Finally, Garmin’s Forerunner 970 is $100 off, costing $649 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI . This is what I’d recommend to marathoners who need something a bit more robust but not as heavy-duty as the flagship Fenix line. I’ve used it to train for a few races and it’s a solid upper-midrange (for Garmin!) option.

item.title: ROUNDTABLE: What Inside NU is thankful for this Thanksgiving
item.description: Folks, happy Thanksgiving! We hope you’re enjoying a much-needed rest from what has been a hectic fall in Northwestern sports. We sure are! But, if you do find some time between playing backyard football and scarfing down some turkey (like many of us are currently indulging in), you should check out what we’re feeling thankful for this year! Once again, happy, happy Thanksgiving! Enjoy! Zac Penson Thankful for: The Ryan Family I could talk about the season Northwestern football started to have under David Braun and Chip Kelly, but after the disaster that the team has become after losing Aidan Chiles, the memory fans will take from this season is the one artifact that will stand as a colosseum on campus for decades to come: the new stadium. The incredible generosity from the Ryan Family is something that myself and ‘Cats fans (as well as probably the away fans that tend to fill our stadium) alike will take away from this season in the long run. It is just an absolutely beautiful stadium that will hopefully lead Northwestern down a path of successful recruitment and cement its place as a legitimate football contender in the Big Ten. If it weren’t for the generosity of the Ryan Family and specifically the effort Pat Ryan Jr. put into the stadium, we wouldn’t have the incredible new Wildcat Wall, the over the top lounges, incredible sight lines, open concourses, the Great Chicago Food Festival, Thunderstruck… the list could go on forever. For all of that, thank you, and Happy Thanksgiving ‘Cats fans! Donovan West Thankful for: Northwestern field hockey I’m not going to lie and say I’m the biggest Northwestern field hockey fan who watched every game this season. There are other diehards on Inside NU that have you covered in that aspect. However, I’m still thankful for our three-time national championship-winning ‘Cats. Not only because they have brought so much pride and glory to Evanston over the past couple of years, but also, selfishly, because it’s a good conversation starter at the Thanksgiving table. When my family asks about NU’s sports, or lack thereof, I run through the typical lowlights of men’s and women’s basketball as well as the head-spinning football and tragedy of Aiden Chiles, but am able to end with, “But hey, the field hockey team just won the National Championship.” So, I’m thankful for the ‘Cats for saving my Thanksgiving conversations. Charlie Jacobs Thankful for: Mark Jackson, the Ryan Family and the Uihlein Family I’m not trying to steal Zac’s thunder at all here, considering I’m writing this after him. Nonetheless, he hit this spot on. The football season started off incredibly hot and has since fizzled out (although that could be a product of the schedule faced and the injury to Aidan Chiles). Northwestern football is on the map now, especially so when there are teams on the cusp of the College Football Playoff that have Northwestern as one of their top wins (Oregon, Iowa, Indiana). item.title: Sexual violence: UK, Mirabel Centre push for stronger protection, justice for survivors
item.description: By Henry Ojelu The United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have renewed calls for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. The British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Mr Jonny Baxter, and founder of the Mirabel Centre, Itoro Eze-Anaba, made the call on Thursday at a special reception and panel discussion in Lagos to mark the centre’s milestone of supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence. The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s landmark publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said although the achievement deserved celebration, sexual violence remained a difficult issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. He said: “We want to celebrate 10,000 survivors, but we also want to ensure that many more people are able to access the professional support and services they need.” The British envoy stressed the importance of placing survivors’ experiences at the centre of interventions, noting that their voices were essential to understanding the challenges they faced and improving access to support and justice. He said the UK remained committed to ending violence against women and girls in all its forms through development partnerships, programmes and collaboration with governments and civil society organisations. Baxter disclosed that the UK would soon host an international summit focusing on technology-facilitated gender-based violence, noting that emerging forms of abuse required new approaches, tools and solutions. He also commended the Mirabel Centre for its pioneering work, describing it as a Nigerian organisation addressing local challenges and changing lives through its support for survivors. Earlier, Eze-Anaba said the centre’s journey could not be told without acknowledging the contributions of the British Council, the Department for International Development and the British High Commission. She disclosed that the British High Commission provided funding for the centre’s first three years and continued to support its work through partnerships and opportunities to advocate for survivors. According to her, the achievement was not merely about the number of survivors supported but the quality, dignity and respect with which services were delivered. “Today is not about public relations for the Mirabel Centre. It is about the services we provide and how those services are shared in a dignified manner for survivors,” she said. Eze-Anaba said the centre regularly sought feedback from survivors to assess its services and identify areas requiring improvement. item.description: Conference League line-ups: Borac vs. Atalanta Atalanta hope Gianluca Scamacca, Jonathan Rowe and Giacomo Raspadori can give them a much-needed Conference League boost away to Borac. It kicks off at the Gradski Stadion Banja Luka in Banjaluka at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET). You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game, Olympiacos-Milan and Juventus-Omonia Nicosia on the Liveblog. BERGAMO, ITALY – NOVEMBER 22: Head coach of Atalanta BC Maurizio Sarri looks on ahead the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and FC Internazionale at New Balance Arena on November 22, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images) It has been a tough season for Atalanta, who on top of adapting to Maurizio Sarri’s radical different style of football, have also been constantly dealing with an injury crisis. They are fresh off a remarkable comeback from 4-2 down to hold Inter 4-4 in Serie A at the weekend. However, they also lost goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi to a serious knee injury that will require surgery. He joins Isak Hien, Odilon Kossounou and third-choice goalkeeper Thomas Pompei on the treatment table, so Marco Sportiello goes in goal. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) There are several other changes, as Nicola Zalewski, Raspadori and Rowe fan out behind striker Scamacca, resting top scorer Nikola Krstovic. The Bergamo boys need points after beating Pafos, then losing 2-0 away to Ajax and held 1-1 by Kairat Almaty. FK Borac Banja Luka have so far secured one win and two defeats in the Conference League. They have Srdan Grahovac not fully fit, and Stefan Savic is a long-term absentee with a torn Achilles tendon. ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Jonathan Rowe of Atalanta BCis challenged by Samuel Chukwueze of AC Milan during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Atalanta BC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 18, 2026 in Italy. item.title: Thanksgiving Classic Entry List Delivers Star Power And Deep Depth
item.description: Former NASCAR Cup Series champion Kevin Harvick, left, and his daughter Piper stand next to Harvick's car before the 13th annual Masters of the Pros 200 race on Wednesday, July 16, 2025, at the Owosso Speedway. Harvick and his 13-year-old son Keelan competed against each other in the race. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The 25th Thanksgiving Classic entry list features 33 Late Model Stock cars packed with champions and past winners ready to race this weekend. Short Track Scene reported the full roster includes defending winner Doug Barnes Jr. and a host of recent tour champions looking to add another marquee title to their shelves. This field proves the event remains the crown jewel of short track racing on the holiday weekend. Seeking another major victory, Kaden Honeycutt brings Truck Series championship pedigree to the No. 17 owned by Kenneth Packer. The depth continues with 2024 CARS Tour champion Brenden Queen returning to the Lee Pulliam Performance No. 03 seat. The Defending Champion Seeks History Doug Barnes Jr. enters as the man to beat after capturing the title last year. He is seeking back-to-back wins in a field that refuses to make it easy. Parker Eatmon joins the fray as the 2024 winner, adding another layer of pressure on the current champ. Chase Burrow and Ronnie Bassett Jr. also bring CARS Tour victory lane experience to the mix. Carson Brown arrives fresh off his South Carolina 400 win and will chase another major trophy in the other Lee Pulliam Performance car. A practice session runs from Noon to 3 p.m. on Friday to let drivers shake down their setups. To secure the top-20 spots, qualifying is set for 3 p.m. on Saturday. Sunday’s pair of last chance races are required for the remaining drivers to earn their positions. A Full Card Of Late Model Stock Action Serving as the fourth race on Sunday night’s card, the main event spans 250 laps. Ultra Broadcasting will air the proceedings live so fans can watch every lap from home. The entry list shows the strength of the Late Model Stock division with drivers like Matt Cox, Keelan Harvick, and Landon Shane Huffman filling out the field. item.title: Cincinnati Bearcats beat Georgia in 1st game of ESPN Invitational
item.description: For Coach Jerrod Calhoun's new Cincinnati Bearcats roster, it was the first non-Ohio road game of the season. Playing in the ESPN Events Invitational at Disney's Wide World of Sports, UC held off Georgia of the Southeastern Conference on Thanksgiving, 83-81. It took a Jayden Hastings block of Georgia's James Scott, followed by his knocking the ball out of bounds for the victory. The Bulldogs made a furious comeback in the second half and the Bearcats had no field goals over the final 2:48. UC led by 16 at halftime and as many as 18 early in the second half, but Georgia came back to take a lead with 6:26 to go on a Kanon Catchings 3-pointer. An MJ Collins Jr. trey put the Bearcats up 75-72 with 3:57 to go and they would not trail from there. The Bearcats led for 31:26 of the 40 minutes. Myles Colvin had 23 points for the Bearcats, all in the first half and Tyler Tejada also finished with 23. Collins had 16 for UC. The Bearcats made just four triples in their last game vs. UMass Lowell . By halftime in Orlando, they were 10-for-14 from the arc. Their previous season-high was 10 in full, 40-minute contests vs. Green Bay and Dayton. UC finished12-for-22, so just 2-for 8 in the second half. They forced 13 Georgia turnovers, 10 in the first half and had nine steals, with eight in the first half. Georgia did dominate on the backboards, 46-33. WHO ELSE?? @mylesjcolvin has 20 and counting in the first half! https://t.co/kH5LUzapvd — Cincinnati Men’s Hoops (@GoBearcatsMBB) November 26, 2026 The Bearcats and Bulldogs played a non-conference game last year in Atlanta, with Georgia winning 84-65. The series lead now goes to UC's only other road game this season was Calhoun's 300th career coaching win at Dayton, 95-72. The Georgia game was another test for UC's 6-foot-10, 245-pound man-in-the-paint, Jayden Hastings. He played 14 minutes with six points, six rebounds and six blocks vs. UMass Lowell . Against the Bulldogs, Hastings had six points, eight rebounds and four blocks, including the game-winner. It was a return home for the senior from Orlando, who had an estimated 20 friends and family on hand. Next up, the Bearcats face his old team, Boston College. The Eagles and UCF battled Thanksgiving afternoon. After battling back from a shoulder injury, Hastings left the game with a bloody nose after being elbowed by Georgia's Donovan Williams on a flagrant foul. Calhoun also started Moeller High's Eric Mahaffey for the first time. Friday, Nov. 27 at 4:30 p.m. (Eastern), it's UC and Boston College on the ACC Network. The Eagles played UCF after UC's Thanksgiving game at Disney's Wide World of Sports. item.title: Patriots vs. Chargers bold predictions for NFL Week 12
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Patriots vs. Chargers bold predictions for NFL Week 12 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots knew that the 2026 season would be a challenge. Certainly it would be more difficult than the one they faced a year ago when the won the AFC East title and ended up in the Super Bowl before losing to the Seattle Seahawks. Their first-place schedule is far more challenging and no opponent was going to take the Patriots lightly. The Patriots come into this Week 12 games having lost three of their last four games and knowing they will be without star QB Drake Maye for at least six more weeks. He fractured his fibula when the Patriots met the Lions in Munich in their Week 10 matchup. The Patriots (5-5) have fallen out of the AFC playoff structure, and they will go into this game against the brutal Chargers (1-9) trying to right themselves. It won’t be easy because they must lean on backup Tommy DeVito at quarterback and a defense that has been largely disappointing. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chargers were expected to fight for a playoff spot and possibly contend for the AFC West title. However, the combination of Jim Harbaugh and Justin Herbert has failed to deliver since starting the season with consecutive home losses to the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders. It has been a flat-out disaster for the Chargers and it’s clear that major surgery is needed on this franchise. The Patriots have played poorly, but they have a chance to fight for a Wild Card spot in the playoffs. They are just one game behind the Cleveland Browns (6-4) and Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4), so opportunities may be ahead if they can start to win. It starts in Week 12 on the road against the Chargers. Tommy DeVito needs quality effort with 175 yards, 1 TD pass Nobody is asking QB Tommy DeVito to turn into a Pro Bowl quality signal caller as he takes over for Maye, but he must deliver the ball accurately and on time. He was able to do that and flash his talent during his previous tenure with the New York Giants, but that “Jersey swagger” has not been a part of his makeup with the Patriots. The likelihood is that he will have opportunities to throw the ball to wide receivers DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Efton Chism along with tight ends Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon. Douglas is the Patriots leading receiver with 32 receptions for 438 yards and 4 TDs, while Henry is the team’s second leading receiver with 34-383-4. Henry is an outstanding third-down and red zone weapon. DeVito may also try to get the ball to Hollins, who has caught 23-294-1. Hollins can make contested catches and could be a key factor in the passing game. item.title: India A player ratings after Rising Stars semi-final exit: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi stands out, Harshit Rana dissapoints
item.description: India A player ratings after Rising Stars semi-final exit: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi stands out, Harshit Rana dissapoints originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India A were eliminated in the semi-final of the Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 after suffering an eight-wicket defeat against Sri Lanka A. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi finished with 281 runs, including a record-breaking 204 against UAE. Prince Yadav and Harshit Rana took seven and eight wickets, respectively, during the tournament, but how do they fare in Cricket News ' ratings? India A knocked out in the semi-finals; fail to win Rising Stars after 2013 India A's campaign in the Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 came to an end with an eight-wicket defeat against Sri Lanka A in the semi-final in Doha. Tilak Varma's side had an inconsistent campaign, losing to Pakistan Shaheens by 48 runs before bouncing back with commanding victories against Nepal and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). However, they could not replicate their best performance in the knockout fixture, with Sri Lanka A chasing down their target of 318 in just 41.3 overs. There were several individual positives despite the disappointing exit. item.title: Contact made: Liverpool star wanted by European club
item.description: Contact made: Liverpool star wanted by European club Virgil van Dijk transfer latest as Trabzonspor make contact over Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk’s future has moved back into focus after fresh reports in Turkey suggested Trabzonspor have opened discussions over a possible deal for the Liverpool captain. According to Hassan Tuncel, there has been “first contact” involving a world-class central defender, with the information pointing towards Van Dijk and communication with his representatives. That development adds another layer to a situation that already feels finely balanced. Van Dijk signed a two-year extension in April 2025, taking his deal through to June 2027, yet uncertainty has persisted. The Dutch defender admitted recently that he has “no idea” where he will play next season, a line that naturally intensified interest across Europe and beyond. Trabzonspor move enters early stage The understanding from Turkey is that Trabzonspor are exploring whether a deal is possible, with an apparent preference on their side to try in the winter window. Van Dijk’s side, however, are thought to favour seeing out the season at Liverpool before any firm decision is taken. Other reports in the same market indicate the timing remains unresolved, with January and next summer both still under consideration. There is also background worth noting. Mohamed Salah joined Trabzonspor in August, with Fabinho following later that month, which has only heightened intrigue around another high-profile arrival. Separate claims have even suggested an offer may already have been put forward, while Van Dijk’s reported valuation stands at €20 million. Liverpool stance still central For now, Liverpool’s position remains the key factor. Van Dijk continues to play a major role at Anfield and recently completed the full 90 minutes in the 4-0 win over Manchester United. His standing inside the squad, his performance level and his leadership mean any decision is unlikely to be taken lightly. Since arriving from Southampton in January 2018, Van Dijk has made 391 appearances and helped deliver every major honour of this era, including two Premier League titles and the Champions League. Interest is understandable. Resolution, though, still appears some distance away. Our View This feels like one to watch calmly rather than one to panic over. Clubs making contact with a player of Van Dijk’s stature is hardly a shock, especially when he is 34 and every move from here carries huge significance. Trabzonspor will see an opportunity, particularly with familiar faces already there, and they are entitled to test the waters. The bigger point is whether Liverpool are ready to move on, and right now that feels far less certain. He is still playing, still leading, still setting standards. When a captain remains that influential, it is difficult to imagine the club rushing towards an exit unless all parties are aligned. There is also a sense that timing matters here. item.description: Europa League line-ups: Juventus vs. Omonia Nicosia Juventus start Francisco Conceicao, Jeremie Boga and Jeff Ekhator in a new 3-4-2-1 formation with Neto in goal as they host Omonia Nicosia in the Europa League. It kicks off at the Allianz Juventus Stadium in Turin at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET). You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game, Olympiacos-Milan and Borac-Atalanta on the Liveblog. GENOA, ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Luciano Spalletti, head coach of Juventus, looks on prior to kick-off in the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and Juventus FC at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on October 28, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) The Bianconeri have done well in the Europa League so far this season, winning every fixture except their 2-2 draw with Stade Rennais. This is a must-win match for their hopes of going through directly to the Round of 16 as one of the top eight teams, but Luciano Spalletti must also rotate the squad. He is still missing Pierre Kalulu, Nico Gonzalez, Kerim Alajbegovic, Khephren Thuram, Manuel Locatelli, Arek Milik and Kamil Grabara, while Edon Zhegrova and Daniele Rugani are not on the UEFA list. Jeff Ekhator and director Giovanni Carnevali (juventus.com) The good news is Juve have Francisco Conceicao back in the starting XI for his first appearance since the shoulder injury on October 18. He is part of a 3-4-2-1 formation with Ekhator as centre-forward and Boga in the trident. Neto also gets his first start in goal for Juventus, albeit in his second spell at the club, having last featured in this jersey in May 2017. Neto joins Juventus – Source: @juventusfc on X Omonia Nicosia sit fourth in their domestic league, and had originally been in the Champions League preliminary rounds, dropping into the Europa League. They started this season strong, beating Celta Vigo and Celje, but then lost 4-1 at home to Benfica and 3-1 away to NEC Nijmegen. They have Fotis Kitsos and Mihlali Mayambela injured, while Carel Eiting, Moses Odubajo, David Akintola and Giorgos Viktoros are cup-tied. Lois Diony is by a long way their top scorer this season with 11 goals in 20 competitive appearances, but only one in the Europa League. item.description: Donnarumma insulted: What really happened with Napoli fans in Manchester Napoli fans once again made their feelings towards Gianluigi Donnarumma clear during Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Manchester City, directing insulting chants at the Italy captain: we talked about it in the latest episode of the Football Italia show. Click here to subscribe to the official Football Italia YouTube channel MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 24: Erling Haaland of Manchester City interacts with teammate Gianluigi Donnarumma during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Manchester City and SSC Napoli at City of Manchester Stadium on November 24, 2026 in Manchester, England. item.title: Orlando Magic serve Thanksgiving breakfast at Coalition for the Homeless
item.description: The Orlando Magic kicked off Thanksgiving by serving breakfast to hundreds of people at the Coalition for the Homeless of Central Florida. The Orlando Magic kicked off Thanksgiving by serving breakfast to hundreds of people at the Coalition for the Homeless of Central Florida. The team hosted its 34th annual Thanksgiving breakfast Thursday morning. Nearly 500 men, women and children who live at the shelter were served, along with more than 100 unsheltered people from the community. First-year head coach Sean Sweeney, who took the job in June, joined the volunteers. As is team tradition, he paid for the meal. Sweeney said he has learned about the franchise’s charitable work since arriving in Orlando. That work includes the annual Orlando Wine Festival & Auction, which benefits the Orlando Magic Youth Foundation. “I think it’s very important,” Sweeney said. Team executives, staff, and former players also volunteered. Several team members said the event helps put the season in perspective. Sweeney continues, “Those guys truly care about the community, and they have a lot of causes that they believe in. So, any time a player, or any of us, have something that we believe in that we think matters we have to do it and we have to do it full speed, with full force. The guys doing (events) around the holidays that mean a lot for them, we encourage it, we support it and we second it.” Click here to download our free news, weather and smart TV apps. item.title: Alexandersson 'overwhelmed' by Swansea interest
item.description: Freyr Alexandersson has only been in charge of Rosenborg since June [Getty Images] Rosenborg head coach Freyr Alexandersson admits he has found it "overwhelming" to be courted by managerless Swansea City and confirmed he has spoken to the Championship side. Ashley Williams is currently interim boss at the Welsh club as they search for a permanent replacement for Vitor Matos following his shock departure to manage French side Strasbourg. Icelander Alexandersson, 44, has only been in charge of Rosenborg since June. The Norwegian top-flight club were in danger of relegation when he was appointed, but are fourth with just three games remaining in the season, which concludes in mid-December. "I can confirm that there is strong interest from Swansea," Alexandersson told Norsk rikskringkasting AS ahead of Saturday's crucial match against Molde, who are just one place behind Rosenborg in the Eliteserien table. "I have heard from them (Swansea), yes... I've never been in this situation before. Even just that is a bit overwhelming. I have strong emotions towards Rosenborg, and particularly the players and the staff that I am working with, so that part is a bit difficult. "But the interest itself from a club in England [sic] which I have said before, it is my dream to be a coach in English football. "That in itself , well I don't know what words I shall use, but it is something I find a bit interesting. "I have no other plans than that I will be standing here tomorrow and hold training, have meetings and preparations ahead of Saturday's match, and be standing at the match on Saturday. "That is what I can say now, because what has happened has happened very fast. And the last 24 hours I have only had focus on Rosenborg. I have had talks with (Rosenborg sporting director Alfred) Finnbogason, so I am only focusing on Saturday's match." Williams to lead Swansea in south Wales derby Alexandersson a contender for Swansea job Middlesbrough beat Swans to go point clear at top Alexandersson previously worked for another Norwegian side, Brann, but was sacked earlier this year after 15 months in charge. Prior to that, he was manager of Belgian side Kortrijk, who are a sister club of Cardiff City - Swansea's arch-rivals who they host in the south Wales derby this Sunday (12:00 GMT). While Alexandersson admits he is unsure whether Swansea have made an official approach to Rosenborg for him, he did confirm that he had spoken to them. When asked if he had been offered the Swansea job, Alexandersson replied: "Well, I cannot comment on that because Rosenborg and Swansea... I don't think there are negotiations even, I don't know what Alfred is saying about it, so I cannot comment. "It is not me who has been hunting for a club. It is them who have come to me and that is of course a great honour to be the one they are hunting for. But Rosenborg... have said all the right things, handled it very, very well and we are trying to take this calmly because anything can happen. It is

item.title: Rewarded for red-hot form! Leeds United tie down free-scoring England striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin to new long-term deal
item.description: AFC Bournemouth v Leeds United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Leeds United have secured the long-term future of Dominic Calvert-Lewin after the striker put pen to paper on a major contract extension. The England international has committed his future to Elland Road until 2029 following a sensational run of scoring form in the Premier League. Commitment amid Manchester United interest Calvert-Lewin has officially signed a new contract at Leeds United, ensuring he remains with the Premier League side until the summer of 2029. The deal comes after a period of intense speculation about his future, with Manchester United among the clubs to have shown interest in the 29-year-old. The club has now officially confirmed the news that had been widely anticipated. Calvert-Lewin arrived at Leeds on a free transfer in the summer of 2025 following his departure from Everton. The striker found the net 15 times in all competitions last season and has already added six goals this term, including one in Saturday's emphatic 4-1 victory over Chelsea. A prolific return to the top flight Since joining Leeds, Calvert-Lewin has scored 19 Premier League goals, making him the highest-scoring English player in the competition during that period. He leads his closest compatriots, Morgan Gibbs-White and Ollie Watkins, by three goals. His impressive performances for Leeds also earned him a return to the England squad in March, with the striker retaining his place in the September/October and November selections. However, he was ultimately left out of England's World Cup squad. Building a core at Elland Road The striker is not the only player committing his future to Leeds, as midfielder Ao Tanaka is also understood to be close to signing a new agreement, according to Sky Sports . Tanaka, who has become a vital component of the midfield, is expected to extend his stay until 2029 as well. The 28-year-old has started nine of the club's 11 league matches this season, and the team's record with him in the starting lineup is formidable, losing just 10 of the 66 games he has featured in from the start. These negotiations follow a busy summer in which several first-team stars, including Ethan Ampadu, Joe Rodon, Jayden Bogle, and Brenden Aaronson, all secured new contracts. Farke remains focused on the pitch While his players are signing new deals, manager Daniel Farke has been less forthcoming about his own contractual situation. The German's current four-year deal is set to expire at the end of the season, despite reports suggesting an agreement in principle has been reached to keep him at the club until 2029. Farke was quick to deflect questions regarding his own future during his most recent press conference, choosing instead to focus on the collective goals of the institution. item.title: What happened to Colston Loveland? Injury update for Bears tight end
item.description: The Chicago Bears were already thin at tight end after losing Cole Kmet due to a season-ending injury. With a top-heavy receiving corps, that puts heavy focus on Colston Loveland after his slow start to 2026. His Thanksgiving performance created more headaches for head coach Ben Johnson. His first quarter fumble erased a potential scoring drive inside the Detroit Lions' red zone . One drive later, Loveland was carted to the locker room for further evaluation from team medical staffers. The culprit? An apparent leg injury that threatens to take him off the field in Week 12 and beyond. Loveland has been declared OUT for the rest of Thursday's game . Now that Loveland can't play, who'll step up for the Bears? Third round rookie Sam Roush is the next man up on the tight end depth chart. He has just six catches for 75 yards this season. He'll be flanked by Stephen Carlson, who has played only 41 offensive snaps over the last four seasons. This article originally appeared on For The Win: What happened to Colston Loveland? Gary Sánchez of the Milwaukee Brewers looks on before Game 4 of the World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026, in St. Petersburg, Fla. Getty Images Last season, Sánchez had a .771 OPS with 12 home runs and 38 RBIs across 86 games. During the playoff run, he appeared in three games and recorded one walk. He mostly served as a backup to star catcher William Contreras but also saw time at DH and first base. Sánchez, who debuted with the Yankees in 2015, spent seven of his 12-year career with the Yankees until 2021. He won both of his All-Star awards while in New York, in addition to his Silver Slugger win in 2017 and he was the runner-up for Rookie of the Year the season prior. Gary Sanchez with the Yankees in 2016. Paul J. Bereswill Gary Sánchez #99 of the Milwaukee Brewers, left, and Christian Yelich #22 pose with the Commissioner’s Trophy in St. Petersburg, Fla., Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. item.title: Charles Barkley’s wild trade take on 76ers’ VJ Edgecombe met with intense ridicule
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Charles Barkley’s wild trade take on 76ers’ VJ Edgecombe met with intense ridicule appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Charles Barkley has suggested that the Philadelphia 76ers trade VJ Edgecombe to improve their bench. Despite Edgecombe embracing a smaller offensive role with the 76ers, Barkley believes Philadelphia could benefit from moving the talented young guard. The Hall of Famer argued that Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey provide enough talent in the backcourt. He believes Philadelphia could use Edgecombe’s trade value to address its depth concerns. “I would trade Edgecombe. I think you gotta find a way to help your bench in Philly,” Barkley said, sharing his surprising trade proposal . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Barkley added that Philadelphia doesn’t necessarily need a third guard alongside Brown and Maxey. His suggestion, however, raises questions about the balance between immediate championship aspirations and long-term success. Edgecombe has already demonstrated his versatility despite playing alongside several established stars. The second-year guard recorded 18 points, six rebounds, five assists, and two steals against the Miami Heat on Wednesday. Philadelphia also improved to 15-4 following its 111-104 victory over Miami. However, Brown suffered a hamstring injury during the contest, highlighting the importance of having additional reliable contributors. The 76ers have previously viewed Edgecombe as a foundational piece, even amid speculation surrounding a potential Giannis Antetokounmpo trade. That makes Barkley’s recommendation particularly surprising. Edgecombe provides athleticism, defensive energy, and scoring potential while remaining under his rookie contract. Trading him for immediate bench help could come at a high long-term cost. Philadelphia would also risk losing a young player capable of developing alongside Maxey. While Barkley’s concerns about roster depth warrant consideration, sacrificing Edgecombe represents a considerable gamble for a franchise balancing its present and future. item.title: Hamilton and Leclerc Hold Fresh Discussions – Cannot Predict Every Scenario in Races
item.description: Lewis Hamilton said on Thursday at the Qatar Grand Prix that he and Charles Leclerc have held positive internal discussions since their Las Vegas collision, while admitting they cannot plan for every scenario in a race. Ferrari needed another set of discussions after the Las Vegas run-in between Hamilton and Leclerc. They held it in Qatar, and Hamilton called it positive. He didn’t share what was discussed, but said it was good for both sides. He spoke to reporters at Thursday’s media day (Nov. 26) in Lusail. Fresh Discussions After Las Vegas “We just had the internal discussions,” Hamilton said to the media. “No, everything stays internal. But good discussions. Positive, yeah. It’s been positive. Charles and I sat here earlier and had a good discussion as well.” Do we need a permanent solution? Yes. But Hamilton put it on Ferrari F1 team principal Frederic Vasseur for any solution. The Brit didn’t wish to add anything else, having already conveyed his thoughts multiple times in the last few weekends. “I mean, that’s for Fred to decide ultimately,” said Hamilton . “I have made my point clear already about them. So yeah, there’s not really much more to say about it really. I said my piece before, and my point hasn’t really changed.” In terms of predicting the scenarios, Hamilton reckons it is not possible to decide about everything for the Grand Prix. They discuss various situations pre-race, but a lot of times things don’t pan out the same way, and collisions still happen. Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc at the Las Vegas GP. Image Credit: Scuderia Ferrari Hamilton Says They Cannot Predict Every Scenario He made clear that he attacks as much as possible, but he is mindful of things, thinking about Ferrari always. “I mean, you can never cover everything because every scenario is different, but definitely you can go through every single race, corner by corner and discuss things that Charles and I have,” said Hamilton. “But yeah, I mean, there’s always going to be something new that you maybe haven’t foreseen, but also, you have to use your instinct, and … also, always the core of it has to be the team. Obviously, I mean, just speaking for myself- when I’m driving, when I’m attacking whoever is on track, I’m always thinking, okay, how is this going to impact everybody behind me, team-wise. “So, I really do try to be as responsible as I can and make the best decision when I am attacking, I think. We’re going to figure it out. We’re teammates at the end of the day, and I think we always learn. We do always learn through these experiences, while maybe it doesn’t necessarily look like it. “But there will be learnings that we take from this difficult period, and I still believe in everything we’re building and working towards in the background,” summed up Hamilton.

item.title: Philadelphia Eagles reporter writes bizarre four-word article on potential Aaron Rodgers signing
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers is back on the free-agent market after leaving the Pittsburgh Steelers, and speculation is building about where he could play next if he does not want to retire. The Baltimore Ravens and New England Patriots have emerged as potential options, as both teams need help at quarterback and are in the hunt for a playoff spot. The Philadelphia Eagles could also be an option after Jalen Hurts was ruled out for the season due to blood clots, albeit their 3-7 record makes a move for Rodgers unlikely. There is also the question of whether teams would want to bring in the 42-year-old amid the controversy surrounding his recent departure from Pittsburgh and his public criticism of head coach Mike McCarthy. One Eagles reporter has made his feelings on the idea abundantly clear. Jimmy Kempski published an article on whether Philadelphia should sign Rodgers, but readers were left with very little to get through. The headline was simply: “Should the Eagles sign Aaron Rodgers?” The entire article consisted of four words: “What? Seriously? God no.” Kempski’s blunt response has gained traction online, with several readers praising the unusual approach. One reader wrote: “Elite article. Concise. Well-written. Accurate.” Another added: “All sports journalism should be written like this. Absolutely perfect. Well done and salute to Jimmy.” A third agreed: “This is what all content should strive to be. Concise, persuasive, insightful. Salute, my dude.” Rodgers’ next destination remains uncertain, but Kempski has made it clear he does not want to see the four-time MVP in Philadelphia. item.title: Lions’ Amon-Ra St. Brown did Ben Johnson’s viral Stanky Leg celebration
item.description: The Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions are squaring off in an epic Thanksgiving Day duel. The two teams share plenty of connections: the Bears’ head coach, Ben Johnson , used to be the Lions’ offensive coordinator. He produced magic with wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and the rest of the Lions offense. Johnson has been celebrating big victories with a viral Stanky Leg celebration, and one Lions wide receiver has seemed to take notice. St. Brown isn’t afraid to talk trash or troll his opponents. item.title: Thanksgiving strut: See rainy, windy Turkey Trots across the US
item.description: As coastal storms bring high winds and heavy rainfall along the East Coast and snow blankets much of the Midwest, countless eager runners woke up early on Thanksgiving Day to celebrate a long-standing holiday tradition: the Turkey Trot. Held across the country on Thanksgiving morning, Turkey Trots offer runners an accessible way to log a few miles during the colder months and give families eager to dress up in turkey hats a chance to come together before a big holiday meal. Turkey Trots feature varying distances but tend to fall around a 5K (3.1 miles) or 10K (6.2 miles). In Chicago, 7,863 runners participated in this year's Turkey Trot, Maddy Rivard, Life Time public relations spokesperson told USA TODAY, despite feels-like temperatures hovering below freezing with wind gusts around 15 mph , according to the National Weather Service. Here's a look at some rainy, windy and even sunny Turkey Trots from Thursday, Nov. 26. See rainy, windy and sunny Turkey Trot photos Greta Cross is a national trending reporter at USA TODAY. Story idea? Email her at gcross@usatoday.com . This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Thanksgiving strut: See rainy, windy Turkey Trots across the US

item.title: What Does Corey Seager’s Future Hold?
item.description: Sep 25, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Texas Rangers shortstop Corey Seager (5) hits a RBI single against the Minnesota Twins in the first inning at Target Field. Mandatory Credit: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor Texas Rangers’ shortstop Corey Seager’s name has been brought up as a potential trade candidate this MLB offseason. Seager is a five-time MLB All-Star, a three-time Silver Slugger, and won the World Series in 2020 with the Los Angeles Dodgers and in 2023 with the Texas Rangers. He won the World Series MVP in both and won the NLCS MVP in 2020. In 2026, Seager batted .227 with 20 home runs, 51 RBI, a .736 OPS and a 3.1 WAR in 102 games. He’s struggled with health in his time with the Rangers, appearing in 119 games per season in Texas. Seager is in the middle of his 10-year, $325 million contract. He could be a potential trade candidate for multiple teams this offseason, so let’s take a look at some potential landing spots for Seager. Sep 18, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Texas Rangers shortstop Corey Seager (5) hits an RBI double against the Toronto Blue Jays during the second inning at Globe Life Field. Mandatory Credit: Raymond Carlin III-Imagn Images Possible Landing Spots for Corey Seager Philadelphia Phillies The Phillies have been linked to Seager if he ends up getting dealt. According to a report, he would be willing to waive his no-trade clause to go to Philadelphia. However, this might not be a great move for the Phillies. They still have Trea Turner, who has seven years and $190 million left on his contract. It would be really hard to swap their salaries, and many teams may want to stay away from Turner. They do, however, need a third baseman after Alec Bohm signed a two-year, $20 million deal with the Kansas City Royals. Seager’s been a shortstop his entire career and only has six career games at third base, all of which came in 2015. A full-time move to third base could potentially help Seager stay on the field more, as third base isn’t as physically demanding as shortstop. If traded to the Phillies, Seager can potentially slot into third base or shortstop if Turner is swapped in the trade. New York Yankees The Yankees were one of the teams in on Seager before he eventually signed with Texas before the 2022 season. Yankee Stadium is commonly known as a “ lefties park” as it has a very short right field at only 314 feet down the line. It’s time for the Yankees to move on from third baseman Ryan McMahon , who’s been poor since the Yankees acquired him at the 2025 trade deadline. Sep 16, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Texas Rangers shortstop Corey Seager (5) bats during the game between the Rangers and the Red Sox at Globe Life Field. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images While the Yankees have multiple lefty bats and aren’t in dire need of a shortstop, New York could be a good spot for Seager. item.title: ‘We wished you stayed longer’ – Nkem Owoh mourns Pete Edochie
item.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Nkem Owoh has paid tribute to his late colleague and friend, Pete Edochie, expressing regret that the legendary actor did not live long enough to celebrate his 80th birthday. Owoh, in a tribute shared on his Instagram page, described Edochie as a dear brother and friend who made people believe in humanity through the way he lived and treated those around him. The actor recalled that Edochie had celebrated his 70th birthday in a special way, during which he spoke about their shared experience in the movie Ikuku . Owoh said he had looked forward to sharing his own story about Edochie when the latter turned 80 on March 7, 2027. However, he lamented that death had taken his friend before the milestone birthday. “I was waiting to tell my own story about you on your 80th birthday, which is on 7th March, 2027. But death had another plan. Who are we to question God?” he wrote. The actor added that he and others had wished Edochie could live a little longer to witness the celebration they had anticipated. “We would have wished you stayed a bit longer to see that great day we were all looking forward to,” he said. Describing the late actor with his traditional titles, including Ogadagidi, Ebubedike and Ononenyi na Nteje, Owoh said Edochie had lived a fulfilled life and prayed for blessings upon his family. “You lived well and we are assured of your place in heaven. Rest well, my friend and brother. May your passing bring immeasurable blessings to your family,” he wrote. He concluded his tribute by describing Edochie as an irreplaceable legend and bidding him farewell with the words, “Ijeoma, Ebube Dike Ndi Igbo.” The post ‘We wished you stayed longer’ – Nkem Owoh mourns Pete Edochie appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Lewis Hamilton confirms "positive" talks with Charles Leclerc after Las Vegas clash
item.description: Motorsport photo Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari's talks since the Las Vegas Grand Prix have been "positive", and believes he and his team-mate Charles Leclerc can move forward together after their latest clash. Leclerc spun Hamilton around while the team-mates fought over sixth place in Las Vegas, three weeks after another clash at the Mexican Grand Prix. Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty and finished 10th, while Hamilton recovered to seventh. Team principal Fred Vasseur called the incident "a lack of respect for the team", and said Ferrari's message after Mexico had been clear. Speaking to the media in Qatar, Hamilton would not go into detail about what had been said since, but made it clear the discussions had gone well. "Everything stays internal. But good discussions," he said. "Positive, yeah. It's been positive. Charles and I sat here earlier on and had a good discussion as well." Asked whether the pair could now move forward in harmony, Hamilton was clear. "I do. I do. We're going to figure it out. You know, we're team-mates at the end of the day, and we do always learn from these experiences, while maybe it doesn't necessarily look like it," he said. Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari "But there will be learnings that we take from this difficult period, and I still believe in everything we're building and working towards in the background." Hamilton said he and Leclerc had already been through every race "corner by corner", but admitted no plan could cover every situation on track. "You can never cover everything, because every scenario is different," he said. "There's always going to be something new that you maybe haven't foreseen. But also you have to use your instinct, and at the core of it, always have to have the team." He believes the difficult moments will make Ferrari stronger in the long run. "These are definitely very, very challenging times for Fred and Charles and I. But these are the moments that you really learn and grow closer together, through conversation and communicating and having those sit-downs," Hamilton said. The Briton also expects to stay in touch with Leclerc over the winter, when the pair are "out of competition" and Leclerc is settling into life as a new father. "I have no doubts that next year we'll come back working hard together and in a better place. We'll hopefully put better processes in place so that we can really elevate the team," he said. Ferrari goes into the final two races second in the constructors' championship, 77 points ahead of Red Bull. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Ojukwu Memorial: Bianca slams South East governors over disunity, rivalries
item.description: . Laments abandonment of Ojukwu by political elite he helped make . Urges Igbo youths in diaspora to shun illicit wealth . As Uwazurike demands Nnamdi Kanu’s release . Insists Biafra struggle must be non-violent By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Ojukwu, has berated Igbo political leaders, particularly governors in the South-East, for failing to unite in the interest of the people, lamenting that their mutual antagonism was undermining the region’s collective progress. This is as the Founder of the Movement for the Actualisation of the Sovereign State of Biafra (MASSOB BIM), Chief Ralph Uwazurike, has renewed his call for the release of the detained Biafra agitator, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, insisting that he committed no offence warranting his continued detention. Bianca, widow of the late Biafran leader, Chukwuemeka Odumegwu-Ojukwu, said the governors had failed to speak with one voice on issues affecting the Igbo, choosing instead to antagonise one another at the expense of the people. She spoke on Thursday at the 15th annual memorial of the late Igbo leader held at the Ojukwu Memorial Library, Owerri, where she called for a departure from political rivalry, personal interests and divisive tendencies. Expressing disappointment with the state of Igbo unity, she said the region could not continue to demand recognition from others while its leaders and people failed to recognise and value one another. “We cannot continue to celebrate Igbo greatness while tolerating the disunity that undermines it,” she declared. The minister lamented that Igbo governors were not sufficiently united to advance the interests of their people, insisting that unity must transcend rhetoric and cultural gatherings to become a practical commitment to regional development. She urged the governors to collaborate for the common good, stressing that the future of the South-East could not be built on mutual suspicion, political antagonism and personal ambition. Bianca also expressed disappointment with some Igbo political elites who, despite benefiting from the influence and political legacy of her late husband, had abandoned him and failed to sustain the ideals he stood for. She said Ojukwu’s legacy should not be reduced to the celebration of his military exploits, titles, speeches and political struggles, but should be understood through his convictions, humanity and commitment to justice and dignity. The minister said her late husband was a soldier, statesman, intellectual and patriarch whose life was driven by a profound belief in justice and the right of people to live without fear. Reflecting on the painful history of the Igbo, particularly the 1966 pogroms, displacement and civil war, she said remembrance of Ojukwu should serve as a commitment to preventing a recurrence of such tragedies rather than merely celebrating the circumstances that made him famous. item.title: Moisés Caicedo, Wesley Fofana available for selection for Chelsea against Nottingham Forest
item.description: JAKARTA, INDONESIA - AUGUST 08: Wesley Fofana and Moises Caicedo of Chelsea FC react after the pre-season friendly match between Chelsea FC and AC Milan at Gelora Bung Karno Stadium on August 08, 2026 in Jakarta, Indonesia. (Photo by Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images) | Chelsea FC via Getty Images Xabi Alonso had some good news in today’s pre-match press conference, confirming that Moisés Caicedo is expected to be fit and available for selection for tomorrow night’s away game against Nottingham Forest. Caicedo was forced off in the first half of last weekend’s match against Leeds United, with his departure, combined with Leeds’ equalizer, resulting in the Blues completely losing our ways and going on to suffer (yet another) rather embarrassing home defeat against historic rivals. “Yes [he’s been able to train], he’s going to be OK for tomorrow.” Unfortunately, the likes of João Pedro and Maxence Lacroix remain out and without a specific timetable for their return. Lacroix’s absence will likely result in yet another game for Wesley Fofana, who continues to frustrate with every appearance, including a recent appearance on a podcast. The reaction to some of the things he said during that 2-hour interview has been less than positive, especially the part where he talked about his performance against Liverpool in the League Cup. But unlike many fans, Alonso considers the case closed now. Fofana apparently apologized for what he said, how he said it, and when he said it. Lesson learned? We’ll have to wait and see. “We have addressed that with him and for sure it was unfortunate. He apologised, he knows it was not right the moment, it was not right the content, we are here to take things seriously and he said that it’s not going to be repeated and we know that it’s something that we don’t want, these kind of things and they are not going to be repeated for sure. [The case is] closed.” -Xabi Alonso; source: Football.London So I guess it’s a question of choosing the least worst option between Fofana and Levi Colwill, who’s had his fair share of terrible outings, plus youngsters like Josh Acheampong or Aarón Anselmino or Olutayo Subuloye. They all have plenty of promise but come with the usual caveats regarding young and inexperienced players. (It would be great if we had some proper veterans to play alongside them, but alas.)

item.title: Maple Leafs Make Significant Changes To Power Play With Marchenko Return
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect He’s baaack. Kirill Marchenko has been desperately missed by the Toronto Maple Leafs over the past month. That’s an understatement. Whether it be 5-on-5 or on the power play, injecting his energy and skill should help a moribund Toronto offense. Granted, looking at Jim Hiller’s practice lines for even strength means absolutely nothing in this Leafs season, as the often-confused coach puts his lines through a blender from nearly the opening puck drop in each and every game. But when it comes to the power play, the way they work on the special teams unit at practice often does translate to the games. And on Thursday, there’s been a significant change to the first power play unit. Kirill Marchenko will immediately rejoin the group as he returns to the lineup for Friday afternoon’s game in Boston. But, as shocking as this may come to followers of the Leafs this season, it will not come at the expense of young Gavin McKenna. No, Marchenko’s placement on PP1 will bump William Nylander off the unit. Accountability is a beautiful thing. https://t.co/vFjR7VOt4s — Nick Alberga (@thegoldenmuzzy) November 26, 2026 As you can imagine, no, Willie is not pleased about the move. “I told him I didn’t agree with it, but that’s okay,” said Nylander. Nylander’s play of late has Leafs Nation up in arms. He hasn’t scored a goal in eight games, is a minus-6 through that period, and has just three points. Then there was the egregious giveaway right out in front of the net in the recent loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets. To his old linemate Matthew Knies, no less. Nylander with an absolute muffin delivery to the former Leaf Knies. No one cares less than William Nylander in Toronto right now What is this pass 😂😂 #Leafs pic.twitter.com/Us4YRujqPm — RGF (@rgfray1) November 22, 2026 Nylander feels his egregious giveaway 2 games ago has led to his demotion Apparently, Nylander believes his demotion to the second power play unit is punishment for that turnover. Hiller responded by saying it’s about making Nylander the “focal point” of the second unit, per Jonas Siegel . Yet somehow, despite that brutal giveaway two games ago, Nylander was still out there being trusted in the final minutes of their first win in 10 games the other night. McKenna, who had actually scored the game-winner midway through the third period, was benched for the rest of that game. There’s simply no figuring out what’s going on in the mind of Jim Hiller. Most of the time, from the puzzling looks and answers he gives the media to some of his moves, it doesn’t seem like Hiller knows what’s going on in there, either. We’ll see how long this new power play arrangement lasts. With Hiller, and with Nylander, anything is possible. item.title: John Harbaugh’s Verdict: Abdul Carter May Play Sunday
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Abdul Carter missed Wednesday’s practice, which sent a wave of worry through the Giants’ locker room and the fanbase. The edge rusher was seen working on a side field with a trainer instead of running with the main group. ESPN’s Jordan Raanan posted on X that Carter was “not in uniform working on a side field with a trainer. Something to keep an eye on.” The same report noted that defensive lineman Shelby Harris and cornerback Dru Phillips also skipped the session. Fans feared a potential blow to the defense just days before a crucial matchup on the road. John Harbaugh quickly shut down the panic with a clear update that the team needed to hear. The head coach told reporters that Carter’s issue is minor and that the player is “day-to-day.” Harbaugh added a definitive line that changes the entire outlook for Sunday: “He should be fine for the game.” This statement comes after Carter was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for his two-sack performance against Jacksonville. The Timing of the Injury Report The Giants have played 10 games so far this season, and Carter has been a consistent force with 26 tackles and four sacks. His ability to generate pressure is vital for a defense that has climbed to the top of the NFC East. Missing a midday practice is often a smart move to preserve a player for the actual game. Harbaugh knows that a full practice session does not guarantee a better outcome than resting a key piece. The coach emphasized that mid-November is the time to get ready for the games that truly matter. A Critical Matchup in Indianapolis The Giants travel to Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 29, to face the Indianapolis Colts. The Colts are 3-8, and New York is a heavy favorite to beat them. However, the Giants must avoid a “trap game” mentality after their recent upset win. Harbaugh has warned his team that they cannot get carried away by the victory over Jacksonville. The defense needs Carter at full strength to maintain the pressure that has defined their play this month. Carter’s injury status remains a key detail to watch as the team prepares for the road trip. While the coach says he should be fine, the final decision rests on how his ankle and calf feel during the week. Per Sports Illustrated , Carter is listed with ankle and calf issues on the injury report.

item.title: Top NFL LB List Backs Eagles’ Confidence In Jeremiah Trotter Jr.
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 28: Jeremiah Trotter #LB24 of the Clemson Tigers speaks to the media during the 2024 NFL Draft Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 28, 2024 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 24: Jeremiah Trotter Jr. #54 of the Philadelphia Eagles hugs his father Jeremiah Trotter prior to the preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings at Lincoln Financial Field on August 24, 2024 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Getty Although Jeremiah Trotter Jr. landed plenty of praise for his progress throughout the offseason with the Philadelphia Eagles, it wasn’t clear that he would become a key player for the defense in 2026. At the start of the season, the Eagles were more focused on Zack Baun and the development of the former first-round pick, Jihaad Campbell. But as Trotter continued to thrive, he couldn’t be denied. Sure, setbacks helped him get more opportunities than expected, but he made it difficult for the Eagles to take him off the field. Pro Football Focus’ rundown of grades for top linebackers in the league this season suggests that the Eagles potentially have a budding star in their 2024 fifth-round pick. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. Grades Out As Top 10 Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – AUGUST 24: Jeremiah Trotter Jr. #54 of the Philadelphia Eagles hugs his father Jeremiah Trotter prior to the preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings at Lincoln Financial Field on August 24, 2024 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) He’s not the best-rest linebacker in Eagles green, but Trotter is next on the list. According to PFF, Trotter grades out at 74.5 for this season so far. He trails Kansas City Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton. Fred. Warner. pic.twitter.com/UNni7TgIma — PFF (@PFF) November 25, 2026 At the start of the season, Trotter played strictly on special teams. It wasn’t until Week 4 that he got significant playing time on defense. His snaps were limited to just 35% in two out of the next three games, but then Trotter played in at least 90% of the defensive snaps over the past three games. This season, Trotter has 64 tackles, with three going for a loss. He got to the quarterback with two hits and landed a half-sack. With Zack Baun out for at least four games, Trotter won’t be going anywhere as long as he’s healthy. He’ll get a chance to keep building and show the Eagles that he was a steal of a pick at No. 155 out of Clemson in 2024. item.title: A flurry of pitcher signings around MLB
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 30: Kevin Gausman #12 of the Chicago Cubs reacts in the National League Wild Card game against the San Diego Padres at Petco Park on September 30, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Matt Dirksen/Chicago Cubs/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we creep closer to the seemingly inevitable MLB lockout that will start at 11 p.m. Central on December 1, 2026, we are seeing a flurry of free agent activity, with teams snatching up starting pitchers, in particular. This year’s free agent class, outside of Tarik Skubal, is pretty uninspiring, low on star power and heavy on middle-class options. Those middle-class options are starting to fly off the board, though. Kevin Gausman, who just wrapped up a five year deal he signed with the Toronto Blue Jays prior to the 2022 season (the final two months of which had him as a member of the Chicago Cubs), reportedly agreed to a 1 year, $25 million deal with the Detroit Tigers. The righthander, who turns 36 in January, was generally expected to get a short-term deal for a lesser annual average value. Gausman provides durability and gets a lot of ground balls, and he is getting more than the $22 million AAV he commanded in his deal with Toronto. Whether this is betting on himself to rebound after putting up a 4.51 ERA — his first 4+ ERA since pre-pandemic — or both player and team being uncertain of what the landscape under a new CBA will look like, and thus giving themselves max flexibility, who is to say. The Colorado Rockies, meanwhile, appear to be trying to corner the market on mid starting pitchers. They reportedly have agreed to terms with David Peterson on a two year, $32 million deal, and with Patrick Sandoval on a three year, $42 million deal. Peterson was projected by Ben Clemens of Fangraphs and Kiley McDaniel of ESPN to land one year deals in the low-teens, while MLB Trade Rumors and the Fangraphs crowdsource median each projected two years at $11-12 million. Peterson got the high end of the range on years and still comfortably exceeded the annual average value projected. The 31 year old 2017 first rounder has posted remarkably consistent xERAs the past four seasons ranging from 4.59 to 4.92, despite a 2.90 ERA and 2024 and a 3.48 FIP in 2025 that produced spikes those years in his bWAR and fWAR, respectively. Like Gausman, he was traded to the Cubs mid-season, and posted a 3.70 ERA for Chicago, compared to a 6.09 ERA for the Mets. His 4.56 xERA for the Cubs was not much better than the 4.97 xERA he put up for the Mets, however, and his 4.06 Cubs FIP was actually worse than his 3.85 FIP for the Mets. Peterson strikes out a below average number of batters and walks an above average number of batters. However, he generates a lot of ground balls, and so maybe the Rockies feel like he’s a better fit in the thin area and big outfield of Coors Field. Patrick Sandoval, meanwhile, did not even make the Fangraphs top 50 free agent list, nor McDaniel’s top 50 list. He did get in

item.title: Wild NFL Proposal Sends Aaron Rodgers to Packers to End Career in Green Bay
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - JANUARY 08: Aaron Rodgers #12 of the Green Bay Packers warms up prior to the game against the Detroit Lions at Lambeau Field on January 08, 2023 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty Aaron Rodgers has only a few weeks left in his NFL career, and one analyst suggests he could go back to where it all started. The Pittsburgh Steelers cut Rodgers loose on Wednesday, capping off a wild and unpredictable 17-hour stretch that started with a late-night announcement that he was being benched. Rodgers then aired the team’s dirty laundry in an interview with Pat McAfee, leveling allegations that head coach Mike McCarthy would fall asleep in meetings and referred to the team as the Packers. Aaron Rodgers Return to Green Bay? Rodgers is expected to clear waivers, where he would be free to sign with any NFL team. That could include a return trip to the Packers, Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox suggested. In an article breaking down the landing spots for Rodgers, Knox listed the Packers as a “break glass” emergency option if starter Jordan Love were to get hurt. Knox noted that Rodgers and the Packers had their own messy breakup, but suggested it wasn’t due to the current regime. “Should the Packers lose starter Jordan Love to injury, a homecoming would make tons of sense for Rodgers and for Green Bay,” Knox wrote. “Rodgers’ first stint didn’t end particularly well, and he essentially forced the Packers to trade him to New York. However, he did spend four seasons under head coach Matt LaFleur and knows his offense well. “Rodgers won a pair of league MVP awards in LaFleur’s system.” While it would require a season-ending injury to Love to make the reunion happen, the Packers might be desperate enough to consider signing Rodgers in that scenario. Green Bay has a very difficult route to the playoffs after losing to the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, dropping their record to 6-5. The Packers may need to win out in order to reach the postseason, and even 12-5 might require tiebreakers given the number of strong teams in their division and NFC West. Aaron Rodgers Could Have More Sensible Option Rodgers could find a more immediate market once he hits free agency, Knox suggested. He noted that the New England Patriots are expected to scan the quarterback market for help after Drake Maye suffered what could be a season-ending injury. “Rodgers is now a part of that market, and his ability to read defenses, make smart decisions, and throw in rhythm would mesh with Josh McDaniels’ offense,” Knox wrote. “While Rodgers has no experience with McDaniels or head coach Mike Vrabel, he does have a history with receivers coach Todd Downing.” Rodgers could also opt to take an early retirement, as he had said prior to the start of the season that this would be his final one in the NFL. India vs. New Zealand 2nd Test, Day 1 Live Score & Updates Welcome to CricketNews.com's live coverage of the 2nd Test between India and New Zealand at Hagley Oval, Christchurch. Toss result: Toss yet to take place. It is scheduled for 10:30 a.m. NZDT (local time), which translates to 3:00 a.m. IST. Pre-match: New Zealand head into the second and final Test against India at the Hagley Oval on Friday with the series still at 0-0. A draw in Wellington did little to help either team's World Test Championship hopes, so the Christchurch match offers both sides a clear chance to make up ground. The first Test had its moments for the visitors, and it could well have ended in their favour. India put together a total of more than 700 on a Basin Reserve surface that offered the bowlers next to nothing, and across five days only 24 wickets fell in 407 overs. KL Rahul added a hundred to the total, while Rishabh Pant also scored a century in the same match, and the home attack was kept in the field for long spells. For India's bowlers, the pitch left little room to force a result, even though Jasprit Bumrah managed to dismiss Latham in the first over of both innings. The hosts have a fitness concern to deal with before the toss, as Blair Tickner has been ruled out of the Christchurch Test with a hamstring injury. Matt Fisher has been called up as his replacement, and he is expected to carry much of the burden of the pace attack on a ground where the ball can be hard to control. However, the bigger worry for New Zealand may be the form of their skipper. Latham was dismissed without scoring in both innings in Wellington, and each time Bumrah removed him in the very first over of the innings. item.title: Stephen A. Smith calls out the NFL after what he saw during Packers’ loss to the Rams
item.description: Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images Fans may have forgotten that there is actually football being played in the NFL amid the media storm that has been created by Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. Wednesday night saw the Los Angeles Rams leapfrog the Seattle Seahawks to the second spot in the NFC West with their victory over the Green Bay Packers. It was a convincing win for Sean McVay’s team, who have finally found their form following the turbulent start to the year. Although focus has quickly reverted back to the situation in Pittsburgh, Stephen A. Smith was keen to vent his frustrations surrounding Kamren Kinchens’ ejection at SoFi Stadium. The ESPN analyst was baffled by the decision to throw the Rams’ safety out of the game. Stephen A. Smith left furious by Kamren Kinchens’ ejection in Rams victory Packers wide receiver Christian Watson suffered a concussion following a big hit from Kinchens. The officials deemed the hit was to the head of the wideout, despite the safety leading with his shoulder. “I don’t agree with that. I did not agree that warranted an ejection or anything like that. I know my brother Ray Lewis is losing his mind, because he’s like, ‘D*** it, we’re men! What are they doing?’ You know, taking everything away from them when it comes to the defence and what it’s allowed to do,” Smith said on First Take. “Do we have that footage of that hit? Do y’all have that? Show that to us, please. Tell me where the illegal hit is on this. What is this? That would seem like a good one to me. Look at that. Come on y’all, right in the shoulders! What’s up? I mean, why is that an ejection? Why?” “It was on the left shoulder, and it was just a devastating hit. He caught the ball, he was in bounds, and I hit him on the shoulder. I just put a hat on him, you know, let him know. I mean, I saw no problem with that hit, zero. At the very least it’s a penalty, not an ejection. I’m like, what are they talking about? It landed on his shoulder. He just got popped silly, that’s all.” The level of officiating has come under real scrutiny this season. This is not even the first time this week that NFL fans have been left frustrated by the referees. Fans were baffled by the Cincinnati Bengals being penalised on Monday night after Joe Burrow was hit late by a Washington Commanders defender. This incident, in particular, only highlights the emphasis the league is putting on protecting so-called defenseless players. However, Travis Kelce has suggested no player should be defenseless when on the field in such a physical game. There are some real concerns over the direction of the game with calls like this being made.
