item.title: Super Falcons: Eguavon invites 24 players for Algeria friendlies
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigeria’s Super Falcons have named a 24 player squad for their upcoming international friendlies against Algeria, with goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie and forward Asisat Oshoala among the key players selected. The squad, announced by interim coach Augustine Eguavoen, will face Algeria on November 30 in Algiers before meeting the North African side again on December 4 in Tizi-Ouzou. Captain Rasheedat Ajibade is, however, absent from the list as she continues her recovery from surgery. The two matches are expected to provide the Falcons with an opportunity to prepare for their Olympic qualifying encounter against Morocco scheduled for March 2027. Nnadozie, Comfort Erhabor and Christiana Uzoma are the three goalkeepers selected for the fixtures. The defensive department comprises Michelle Alozie, Shukurat Oladipo, Glory Ogbonna, Oluwatosin Demehin, Glory Edet, Valentina Uroko and Nicole Payne. In midfield, Eguavoen has called up Christy Ucheibe, Joy Igbokwe, Regina Otu, Fatimoh Solaty, Suliat Abideen, Toni Payne and Jennifer Echegini. Oshoala will lead the attacking options alongside Folashade Ijamilusi, Shakirat Moshood, Blessing Okpe, Joy Omewa, Blessing Nkor and Olamide Adugbe. The friendlies form part of Nigeria’s preparations as the team looks to secure qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games. item.title: NDC using ‘rig and die’ slogan to mobilise for mass rigging – Keyamo
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo SAN, has accused the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC of using the “rig and die” slogan as a cover to mobilise its members and “rig the elections massively.” Keyamo made the claim on Thursday in a post on his X account. He was reacting to a clarification of the slogan by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi. “There is no need for Peter Obi to clarify the ‘rig and die’ slogan and do damage control. We know what it means. The slogan is nothing but a subterfuge for them to mobilise themselves and rig the elections massively as they did in a part of the country in 2023 but still failed”, he said. The minister asked what would stop a party that is “sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents” from rigging elections itself. “If a party in a contest with other parties is sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents, what stops that same party from rigging the elections itself? Are they saints?” he asked. He argued that no party can be both contestant and referee. “You cannot be a participant in a contest, yet you want to act as the umpire under the guise that you don’t trust the umpire! That is creating a graver absurdity than the one you’re trying to solve!” he said. The slogan became a national talking point after a former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District, used it at a campaign event in Uvwie, Delta State, in October. “Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him!” Omo-Agege said, adding: “It is rig and die.” Tension over the slogan grew after gunmen attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign team at Uduere, in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, this Monday. His media adviser, Sunny Areh, said four people were killed and four others critically injured, while Omo-Agege was unhurt. Other reports put the death toll at six. Keyamo condemned the killings the same day. He asked promoters of the slogan to “publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature.” “It is wrong to tell your supporters to kill other citizens under whatever guise. It smacks of desperation,” he said then. Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, later visited the families of the victims. Obi also spoke to Channels Television on the slogan. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die,'” he said. Obi was also reported to have said that the slogan “simply means, do not rig the election. We want a free and fair election. It never meant campaign and die.” He also defended supporters of the Kwankwasiyya movement, who carry sticks to political gatherings. He said they have never used them to harm anyone. However, Keyamo dismissed the explanation, saying Obi’s camp was the one casting itself as the aggrieved party. “This is a classic case of the villain playing the victim,” he said. item.title: Indie web browser Ladybird enters alpha testing
item.description: The independent Ladybird web browser has reached an important milestone: an alpha test version. What's more, it works well. These may not be the criteria by which some will judge it, though. Earlier this week, the developer behind the Ladybird web browser announced that Ladybird is now in alpha . We've given it a brief test, and it performed very well. It's more stable and works better than its alpha label would suggest. There are downloads available , covering macOS on Apple Silicon, as well as for Linux on x86-64; for the latter, there's a Flatpak package, as well as native Ubuntu and Fedora packages. It's an open source project, so you can download the source code from the GitHub repository and compile it yourself, but in an unusual move, back in June the project announced that the developers would no longer accept public code contributions. We first mentioned Ladybird as part of our early 2022 look at its original parent project – SerenityOS: Remarkable project with its own JS-capable web browser . Both the name and the date are significant: the former is a nod to the Serenity prayer , recited at the end of Alcoholics Anonymous meetings. The date of the article is because it's well before the launch of ChatGPT at the end of 2022 . About a year and a half later, we reported that Serenity OS turns five and emits first offspring, Ladybird . Both the OS and the browser were still hand-coded, but now the browser could be compiled and run on other OSes. That freed it up to call upon external libraries which didn't exist for SerenityOS. Earlier this year, we wrote Ladybird flutters toward Rust with a little help from AI . At one point, developer Andreas Kling used Apple's Swift language, but this year, he changed course and adopted Rust instead, using LLM tools to convert some existing code. Some will dismiss Ladybird because of this, but as our first coverage shows, the browser and its original host OS were established projects before the current wave of AI-assisted development. Kling does use LLMs, but Ladybird is not some sloppy vibe-coded effort. The macOS download is 68.4 MB in size, which in 2026 is remarkably small. The Flatpak is larger – about 111 MB – but it also pulls in some KDE dependencies which increase its size. We tested it on Pop!_OS. It handles sites such as The Register and Hacker News and everything else we tried perfectly, and took just 6 percent of our Dell XPS13's CPU to play full-screen HD video from YouTube smoothly. In our short testing, we saw no crashes, hesitation, or any other problems at all. The developers nevertheless warn that the alpha can crash, some websites will not work, and they make no security guarantees at this stage. The use of LLMs will put some people off. However, this is not the only controversial thing about the project. As we have noted in our previous coverage, Ladybird belongs to the same political wing of the FOSS movement as Omarchy, XLibre, and other right-wing projects. If the LLM use doesn't

item.title: Aubameyang escapes injury in car crash ahead of Barcelona clash
item.description: Deportivo La Coruña striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang escaped unhurt after his car was involved in a collision with another vehicle while he was driving to the club’s training ground on Thursday. The incident occurred at about 9:23am on the AP-9 motorway in the Piadela area, near the junction with the A6, according to Spanish newspaper Marca. Both vehicles sustained damage, but nobody involved in the accident was injured. Aubameyang continued his journey to Deportivo’s Abegondo training base after the collision and joined his teammates for the scheduled group session. The Gabon international later played down the incident, describing it as a minor scare and expressing relief that everyone involved was safe. “It was just a little scare. These things happen in life. The most important thing is that the other person involved in the accident is fine, and so am I,” he said. The incident comes as Deportivo prepare to host Barcelona at the Riazor Stadium next Sunday, a fixture that will see Aubameyang face his former club. The striker had recently returned to action after recovering from a knee injury that kept him out for a period. He resumed playing at the beginning of November, gradually increasing his involvement in the team. He also experienced ankle discomfort during training last week and underwent medical examinations before recovering sufficiently to travel with the squad for their match against Alavés in Vitoria. Aubameyang had made an impressive start to the season, scoring five goals in his first five official appearances before the knee injury interrupted his run. His availability will be important to Deportivo as they prepare for the Barcelona encounter, with the club relying on his experience and attacking contribution. item.title: Navy dismantles four illegal refineries, recovers 112,525 litres in Rivers
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has dismantled four illegal refining sites and uncovered approximately 112,525 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) in separate operations in Rivers State. The Director of Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this on Thursday, saying the operations exposed repeated attempts by oil thieves to reactivate previously dismantled illegal refining sites. He said the operations were conducted on November 25, 2026, by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Soroh and Forward Operating Base (FOB) Bonny in Ogbogolo Community, Ahoada West Local Government Area, and George Pepple Community, Bonny Local Government Area. According to him, personnel of NNS Soroh discovered two illegal refining sites at Ogbogolo, containing approximately 15,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and 525 litres of suspected illegally refined AGO. The sites also contained three cooking drum ovens, two dugout pits and other equipment used for illegal refining activities. In a separate operation at George Pepple Community, Folorunsho said personnel of FOB Bonny discovered two illegal refining sites comprising 13 dugout pits. He said seven of the pits contained approximately 97,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil, while four contained water and two were freshly excavated. Folorunsho said all identified facilities and recovered petroleum products were handled in accordance with established procedures. He noted that the operations exposed continued attempts by oil thieves to relocate and reactivate illegal refining activities following previous military operations. “By targeting the facilities used for processing and storing stolen petroleum products, the Nigerian Navy is constraining the operational capacity of criminal operators and disrupting activities that undermine the country’s oil and gas industry,” he said. The Navy spokesman reiterated the service’s commitment to sustaining operations against crude oil theft, illegal bunkering and related criminal activities, particularly to protect critical oil and gas infrastructure. He added that the operations were aimed at safeguarding Nigeria’s energy resources and national economic interests. item.title: 2027: Nwifuru, Umahi, Anyim rally support for Tinubu
item.description: …Umahi targets 1.3m votes, warns against hate speech By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru; Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Anyim Pius Anyim; and former Nigerian Ambassador to Greece, Chief Franklin Ogbuewu, have mobilised support for President Bola Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. They declared their support on Thursday during the APC’s state campaign flag-off in Afikpo Local Government Area of Ebonyi State. Addressing supporters at the event, Nwifuru described the APC as a comprehensive political party with candidates for all elective positions in the state and urged residents to vote for Tinubu and other party candidates. The governor commended Tinubu for what he described as massive infrastructure development in Afikpo and urged residents to reciprocate the President’s efforts through their votes in 2027. “We are campaigning for all our candidates, beginning with the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “On January 16, 2027, you will be voting for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. What you will see on the ballot is the symbol of our great party, the broom. That broom represents the unity that has brought us together and sustained the peace we enjoy. “When you thumbprint on the broom, you have voted for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. On the same day, you will also vote for our senatorial candidate, Professor Anthony Okorie, a distinguished scholar and accomplished academic. “You will equally vote for our own brother, a very calm, resilient, committed and unassuming person, Elumakama Joseph, who is our House of Representatives candidate,” he said. Nwifuru appealed to political leaders and residents of Afikpo to support all APC candidates, arguing that his ability to represent the state effectively would be strengthened by Tinubu’s re-election. “I am not asking you to vote for me alone. I want you to understand that voting for me without voting for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will not serve our collective interest. “If you vote for me without supporting President Tinubu, I will not have the necessary political leverage to represent you effectively before him,” he said. The governor further urged residents not to take the Federal Government’s projects in the state for granted, claiming that no previous administration since independence had initiated and commissioned infrastructure projects in Ebonyi on the scale of the Tinubu administration. In his remarks, former SGF Anyim urged residents to demonstrate their support for Nwifuru by voting for Tinubu and other APC candidates. He also called on eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate in the elections. “Everybody should get ready. Collect your PVCs and ensure that you defend your votes. item.title: Lawal reaffirms refusal to negotiate with bandits
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has reiterated his administration’s decision not to negotiate with bandits terrorising the state, insisting that efforts would instead focus on reclaiming ungoverned areas and restoring security. Lawal stated this on Thursday at the graduation ceremony of the Zamfara Forest Guards held at Government Secondary School, Gada Biyu, Gusau. More than 1,000 forest guards graduated after undergoing training in weapons handling, physical fitness, combat readiness, civil-military relations, security cooperation, community engagement and the rule of law. The armed forest guard initiative was launched by President Bola Tinubu on May 24, 2025, to train residents to secure forests and other ungoverned areas across the country. At the ceremony, Lawal expressed appreciation to Tinubu and the National Security Adviser for the Federal Government’s support for the initiative. He also commended security agencies, the training coordinator and instructors for their roles in preparing the guards for service. Addressing the graduates and their families, the governor said Zamfara needed to reclaim its vast ungoverned areas, which he said had become hideouts for bandits and other criminal groups. “We must urgently reclaim Zamfara’s vast ungoverned areas, which have become safe havens for bandits, criminals and terrorists. “This will require sustained cooperation between federal and state authorities, a reliable security presence and the restoration of public services. “Our goal is to ensure displaced families can return safely, and communities can farm, trade and rebuild their livelihoods,” he said. The governor said his administration had invested substantially in security agencies over the past three years through the provision of operational equipment, vehicles, surveillance technology and logistical support. He listed the equipment provided to security agencies as more than 30 Armoured Personnel Carriers, 200 operational pick-up vehicles, 20 Toyota Buffalo vehicles and over 1,000 specialised motorcycles. He added that additional vehicles and motorcycles had also been supplied to the Homegrown Community Protection Guards. On surveillance, Lawal said the state had acquired drones, including an 80-metre endurance model capable of covering up to 50 kilometres and operating continuously for eight hours. According to him, the equipment would improve reconnaissance, situational awareness and coordination in difficult terrain. Reaffirming his administration’s position on negotiations with armed groups, the governor said: “I want to make it clear again, we are still firm in our decision never to negotiate with the criminals.” The post Lawal reaffirms refusal to negotiate with bandits appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again
item.description: Sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car. In the years since, the Blue Oval has been back to France more than a few times, with varying success. It could never replicate the GT40’s success winning overall, but it celebrated the 40th anniversary with a class win . Now it wants another shot at the really big trophy , and it debuted the car during the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears football game today: meet the GT41. “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It's the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.” The video was directed by Zack Snyder and features Matt Damon’s voice-over. Like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars. LMDh cars start with one of four approved carbon fiber chassis—in this case, Ford is working with Oreca, which has also partnered with Genesis and Acura. Read full article Comments

item.title: 'Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home' at 40: 'Trek' has never been as joyous or fun as in 'the one with the whales'
item.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters. They gave him freedom to tell the story he wanted to tell, and he landed on a not obviously box-office-friendly formula of "No dying, no fighting, no shooting, no photon torpedoes, no phaser blasts, no stereotypical bad guy". It was a massive shift away from Khan and Kruge, the grandstanding villains in movies II and III. Nimoy also wanted the film to have an environmental message and appeal beyond the franchise's traditional fanbase. The film would actually be promoted with minimal "Trek" branding in some territories. (Image credit: Paramount) "I wanted to make it accessible to people who don't go to 'Star Trek' movies," Nimoy said in "The Fifty-Year Mission" by Edward Gross and Mark A. Altman. "I wanted to make it a movie-movie. It starts out like a 'Star Trek' movie and then makes a left turn. It is intentionally very different." "The Voyage Home" effectively closes the trilogy that began four years earlier with "The Wrath of Khan". The story picks up three months after Spock's regenerated body is reunited with his katra (spirit), though nobody ever explains why Kirk and the rest of the crew are all still wearing exactly the same clothes. Following the self-destruction of Enterprise over the Genesis Planet, the gang are heading back to Earth to face the music for a lengthy rap sheet that includes grand theft starship and insubordination on an epic scale. But as they voyage home (geddit?) in a reconditioned Klingon Bird-of-Prey nicknamed the Bounty — complete with a cloaking device that wil

item.title: Fofana apologises over unauthorised interview; Alonso says issue is closed
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso says Wesley Fofana has apologised for giving an unauthorised interview in which he laughed about the penalty miss that knocked the club out of the Carabao Cup against Liverpool. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of Friday’s Premier League game against Nottingham Forest, Alonso said the matter had been addressed and Fofana would be available to play. “We have addressed that with him and for sure it was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it wasn’t the right moment. The content wasn’t right,” Alonso said. “We are here to take things seriously and he said it wouldn’t be repeated. We know it’s something we don’t want and they are not going to be repeated.” In the interview with French YouTuber Zack Nani, Fofana said he could “laugh about” the penalty miss. The defender also spoke about having considered retiring from football during one of his spells out with injury at Chelsea. Alonso also urged his players to respond to their 4-1 defeat by Leeds, saying they had failed to meet the standards required to compete. “On Saturday, we missed not just players but many basics to compete in the game. That’s been clear during the week,” he said. “We talked about having those basics to compete, to know what it takes to be ready for each game and we will need that tomorrow.” He said the defeat had been analysed but should not be forgotten. “The idea is that we don’t forget. In the future, we’ll say those standards are not acceptable at this level.” The post Fofana apologises over unauthorised interview; Alonso says issue is closed appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC to test BVAS in 406 Ondo polling units
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will on Saturday conduct a mock test of its voter accreditation technology in Ondo State ahead of the 2027 general elections. The exercise will take place in 406 polling units across the state’s 18 local government areas between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. INEC said the exercise was designed to assess the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and identify potential technical challenges ahead of the general elections. In a statement, the Deputy Director and Head of Department, Voter Education and Publicity, Olayinka Ogunseye, said two polling units had been selected from each of the 203 registration areas in the state. The Commission explained that the test would assess how the BVAS performs under different conditions and enable it to address any technical issues identified before the elections. INEC stressed that the exercise was not an election, adding that no voter would cast a ballot for any candidate or political party. It urged residents of the affected polling units, community leaders, political parties, civil society organisations and journalists to cooperate with its officials to ensure a successful exercise. The Commission also cautioned against the spread of rumours and fake news, urging residents to obtain election-related information only through its official communication channels. It said the mock accreditation exercise was part of its early preparations to ensure the smooth deployment of technology and the conduct of credible elections in 2027. The post INEC to test BVAS in 406 Ondo polling units appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Atiku tackles Tinubu over rising cost of production, housing
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of worsening Nigeria’s cost-of-living crisis through rising energy and production costs. Atiku said expensive and unreliable electricity was forcing manufacturers to spend more on production, pushing up the prices of goods and making homes increasingly unaffordable. In a statement on Thursday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku cited reports that 11 listed manufacturing companies spent ₦842 billion on energy in the first nine months of 2026, describing the figure as evidence of the burden of unreliable and expensive power. “₦842 billion is the energy bill of only 11 companies in nine months. Cement manufacturers are among the industries hit hardest by the cost of power. That cost does not disappear at the factory gate. It enters the price of every bag of cement and pushes the cost of building a home further beyond the reach of ordinary Nigerians,” he said. Atiku also questioned the Tinubu administration’s claim that it had delivered more than 26,000 housing units, arguing that the figure included unfinished projects and developments initiated under former President Muhammadu Buhari. He noted that 10,328 of the reported units were still under construction and demanded a breakdown of inherited projects, completed houses and those occupied by beneficiaries. “A building site is not a completed home. An inherited project is not proof of fresh delivery. A mortgage approval is not a house key. Publish what Tinubu inherited, what his administration completed, how many families have moved in and what those homes cost,” he said. He also challenged the administration’s claim that its housing programme had generated 525,100 construction jobs, arguing that projected employment opportunities should not be presented as jobs already created. On the wider economic impact, Atiku said the rising cost of energy was forcing manufacturers to increase prices, reduce production, delay expansion or cut jobs, with consumers bearing the consequences. “When factories spend fortunes on electricity, diesel and gas, they raise prices, cut production, postpone expansion or shed jobs. Families then pay more for everything those factories produce. Tinubu’s energy failure is being added to every Nigerian’s bill,” he said. Atiku said his Affordable Life campaign would prioritise reliable electricity for industries and a transparent, targeted subsidy for domestically refined fuel to reduce production costs and ease the burden on consumers. He said the government could not promise affordable housing while the cost of building materials remained beyond the reach of ordinary Nigerians. “You cannot build affordable homes with cement that families and builders can no longer afford. You cannot protect jobs while factories spend fortunes generating their own power. And you cannot res

item.title: How I was attacked by gunmen, says Edo NDC victim
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – A member of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), who sustained gunshot injuries along Airport Road in Benin City while awaiting the arrival of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has recounted how he was attacked by gunmen. The victim, Aimionkhale Michael, narrated his experience to journalists at the hospital where he is receiving treatment. Michael, a youth leader from Uromi in Esan North-East Local Government Area and an aide to the NDC House of Representatives candidate for Esan North-East/Esan South-East Federal Constituency, Akhakon Anenih, said he was among party supporters who had gone to the airport to welcome Obi, who was in Edo State for a town hall meeting. He said the supporters remained outside the airport gate because of the heavy security presence. According to him, the scorching sun forced him to seek shelter inside a vehicle while waiting for the presidential candidate’s arrival. “The sun was scorching, so I decided to relax inside the vehicle, with the intention of joining the convoy when they come out,” he said. He alleged that shortly before the shooting, an unidentified man approached him and asked for a fez cap, claiming to be an NDC supporter. Michael said shortly after the man left, a black Toyota Hilux arrived, and its occupants allegedly opened fire indiscriminately. “I told him I didn’t have any cap to give him. Shortly after he left, I saw a black Hilux van. The occupants were shooting and firing everywhere. They shot me at close range on my thigh while I was inside the vehicle. The bullet penetrated my left thigh to the right one,” he said. He said a female police officer and other security operatives rushed him to the hospital after he managed to get out of the vehicle and cried for help. “Immediately, the medical team took me to the theatre, where they commenced treatment. I thank God for sparing my life. I don’t know my attackers or what they are looking for,” he said. He called on the authorities to identify and arrest those responsible for the attack, insisting that political differences should not be allowed to fuel violence. “They should fish out those hoodlums and ensure they are brought to justice. People should understand that elections are not about violence. We are all brothers and sisters, and thugs should not be used to perpetrate violence all in the name of elections,” he added. item.title: FG targets stronger local capacity for energy security
item.description: By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — The Federal Government has expressed its readiness to strengthen local industrial capacity, infrastructure and investment as part of efforts to achieve energy security and accelerate Nigeria’s economic transformation. The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, said energy security went beyond the availability of natural resources to include the capacity to produce, process, transport and distribute energy reliably and affordably for the benefit of citizens. Akume spoke in Port Harcourt at the 10th Africa Energy Summit, organised by the Solewant Energy Training Institute, a subsidiary of Solewant Group, with the theme, “Scaling Innovative Industrial Capacity for Africa’s Energy Security.” Represented by his Special Assistant on Technical Matters, Prof. Babatunde Benerd, the SGF said Nigeria’s ambition for economic growth, industrialisation and job creation depended on an energy system capable of meeting the needs of households, businesses and industries. He said the administration of President Bola Tinubu considered reforms in the energy sector, investment and industrial development critical to the country’s economic transformation. “The current administration is pursuing reforms aimed at improving the investment climate, strengthening domestic production and creating conditions for productive activities,” he said. Akume said the implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act had provided a framework for improved governance, clearer institutional responsibilities and increased investment across the oil and gas value chain. He added that the government was promoting domestic gas utilisation, compressed natural gas development, investment in energy infrastructure and reforms in the electricity sector. The SGF stressed that local content should go beyond Nigerian participation in petroleum projects to building competitive enterprises capable of manufacturing products, providing specialised services, creating jobs and competing internationally. Also speaking, the Special Adviser to the President on Energy, Olu Verheijen, represented by Dr Olusegun Amoda, said recent reforms in the sector had helped restore investor confidence and attract fresh investments. Verheijen said the administration had introduced executive orders and policy directives to provide fiscal incentives for investors, reduce contracting timelines and costs, and strengthen local content in the petroleum industry. She said the reforms had contributed to investment decisions worth more than $8 billion in oil and gas projects, adding that improved regulatory stability and security in the Niger Delta had helped create a more favourable investment climate. According to her, oil and gas projects require fabrication, engineering, drilling services, equipment, logistics and maintenance, creating opportunities for local businesses across the value chain. item.title: Ex-BBC commentator Starmer-Smith dies aged 81
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former England scrum-half and renowned BBC rugby commentator Nigel Starmer-Smith has died aged 81 after a long battle with dementia. His son, Charlie, announced his death in a social media post on Thursday, saying he had “passed away peacefully this morning”. “Dad passed away peacefully this morning after a long battle with dementia,” Charlie wrote. Starmer-Smith was diagnosed with dementia in 2015. In 2021, Charlie described the condition as a major issue in sport and recalled how Covid-19 restrictions meant the family could only see his father through a window. The son also said head injuries were once treated as “like a badge of honour” in rugby and that dementia had affected other members of their family. Starmer-Smith played for Harlequins and the Barbarians and won seven England caps between 1969 and 1971. After retiring in 1976, he moved into broadcasting and journalism. He voiced the BBC’s Rugby Special highlights programme for 15 years and later commentated for ITV at the 2003 Rugby World Cup in Australia, where England won the title. In his tribute, Charlie described his father as “one of life’s great tourists” and remembered him as a player, commentator, writer, charity fundraiser, volunteer and family man. “He was a modest man and he’d hate for people to make a fuss,” Charlie wrote. “He loved to laugh but not as much as he loved to see others laughing.” He urged those who knew his father to think of a happy memory and smile, saying that was how he would remember him. item.title: 2027: Barau mobilises 3,405 Kano traditional rulers for APC
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, has mobilised 3,405 traditional rulers in Kano State to support President Bola Tinubu, Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, himself and other candidates of the All Progressives Congress, APC. The meeting, held at the Ali Jita Event Centre in Kano, brought together 3,032 ward heads, 347 village heads and 26 representatives and secretaries of district heads. According to a statement issued on Thursday by Barau’s Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ismail Mudashir, the engagement was part of the senator’s ongoing consultations with stakeholders across Kano North Senatorial District. The meeting came barely 72 hours after Barau rallied more than 2,000 Islamic clerics from the 13 local government areas of the district to support Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections. Mudashir said the Deputy Senate President had, in recent months, intensified consultations with critical stakeholders across Kano North, urging them to support the President and all APC candidates. Barau commended the traditional rulers for their contributions to grassroots development, describing them as important partners in promoting peace, security and the wellbeing of their communities. He also appreciated their cooperation and prayers, saying traditional institutions remained closest to the people and understood their needs and challenges. On security, the senator acknowledged the challenges confronting some communities in Kano North but expressed optimism that the situation was improving through the collective efforts of security agencies and other stakeholders. He said the deployment of an Army battalion to Dambatta Local Government Area, in addition to existing security formations across the district, would strengthen security and protect lives and property. Highlighting electricity projects across the district, Barau said projects in Bichi, Dawanau Market and Kwanar Kanye in Kabo would cost more than N130 billion. “These projects may take time, but they will definitely turn around the economic fortunes of our senatorial district. I remember when I was in the House of Representatives between 1999 and 2003, similar power projects were attracted to Ogun State by the former President. Today, the state has become an industrial hub. We will get there in Kano North too,” he said. He said the electricity projects, alongside the Federal University of Science and Technology, Kabo; Police Training School; Immigration Training School; and Civil Defence Training School, would stimulate economic activities, create jobs and accelerate development. In the health and education sectors, Barau disclosed plans to upgrade the Bagwai and Kabo hospitals into major referral and teaching hospitals, with the Kabo facility expected to serve as a teaching hospital for the Federal University of Science and Technology. item.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
item.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. From L-R: Oluwatomi Otuyemi, Senior PR Account Manager, M.Inc PR; Tamunotonye Waka

item.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
item.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®

item.title: Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
item.description: null Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . Stargazers in the U.S. could get an incredible view of Venus in the predawn hours of the coming week, as the planet climbs into the southeastern sky ahead of the rising sun, with Mercury clinging close to the horizon below. Celestron Nexstar 4SE (Image credit: Celestron) This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. For a closer look at craters and the terminator, make sure to grab a 9mm or 12mm eyepiece and get stronger magnification. _ Celestron Nexstar 4SE review The bright star Spica will glow less than five degrees away from Venus before dawn on Nov. 27 — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length against the night sky. Spica is a double system of two stars that orbit one another once every four days. Its stars are separated by just approximately 11 million miles (less than 18 million kilometers), making them far too close to split visually with even the most powerful amateur equipment. However, the system still makes for a dazzling target, appearing as a magnificent blue-white star when viewed through the eyepiece of a 4-inch telescope. Venus will appear close to Spica in the southeastern sky. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) Check that the sun is safely below the horizon before turning your telescope on Venus to observe a crescent of light playing across the planet's dense atmosphere. Over the coming weeks and months, Venus will appear increasingly illuminated as it moves farther away from Earth in its orbit, while its apparent size through a telescope will gradually decrease. Want to get a closer look at the planets of the solar system and the stars beyond? Then be sure to check out our roundups of the best telescopes and smart telescopes for observing the night sky. item.title: Spurs latest: Savio set for several weeks out
On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
item.description: null On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. (Image credit: collectSPACE/Robert Z. Pearlman ) Why it mattered It may be hard to imagine now, but 15 years ago, the idea of a nuclear-powered rover on Mars was just a concept. When the Curiosity rover launched in 2011, it made that idea a reality the car-size probe (using a plutonium-based radioisotope thermoelectric generator that converts heat from radioactive decay into power) as it headed to the Red Planet. Curiosity was the largest rover ever launched to Mars, following up on the success of the tiny Sojourner rover in 1997 and the larger twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity in 2004. Its sky crane landing system was novel at the time, and fully automated. Once it began its descent in August 2012, NASA could only wait through "seven minutes of terror" to see how it turned out. It ended being a huge success. NASA's Curiosity rover on Mars. (Image credit: NASA) After its smooth landing, Curiosity lived up to its original name: the Mars Science Laboratory. Within weeks, Curiosity fulfilled its primary mission. It found evidence of ancient running water on Mars . It later found organic molecules on Mars as well. Curiosity's primary mission was expected to last just about one Martian year (687 Earth days, or about two Earth years), as the rover explored its Gale Crater landing site. But NASA has extended the mission as the rover continues to operate in good health. In fact, Curiosity has survived long enough to welcome its successor to Mars, the Perseverance rover , which landed in February 2021 on a mission to collect the first samples for later retrieval. Perseverance used the same basic 2-ton design, plutonium power system and sky crane landing system to reach Mars. And today, a ground-based twin of the Curiosity rover, called Promise , is being outfitted for an upcoming mission to the moon. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Detty December Finds Its Crown: Green Indie Artistry 2026
item.description: There is a burst of energy and undeniable excitement that comes over a room when the crowd realises it has power. It happened at BallR Lagos in December 2024, when Green Indie and Hennessy staged the first Indie Star Search finale. The lights dropped, the names were read, and the verdict was something the audience helped write. On Thursday, 17 December 2026, that idea returns bigger. Green Indie Artistry opens at 5:00 PM at Baywater Park, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos. The headliners are 9ice, Fido, and JAYBERRY . Four DJs keep the floor moving between sets. And at the center of the night sits the Indie Star Search, where four finalists perform for the people who will decide who wins. It is less a concert than a referendum with a dance floor. The Premise: Judged by the Room Most competitions are decided behind closed doors. Green Indie flips that. Four finalists perform live, and everyone holding a pass votes on the sets. That audience vote carries its weight in the result. The format has a sharp edge. The people who paid to be in the room become accountable for what happens in it. If the winner is an artist you championed from the front, you helped put them there. The competition has history. The inaugural Indie Star, Young Incredible, won in 2024 with “Lagos to Abuja” and walked off under a storm of confetti. The four finalists for 2026 will be revealed on 6 December. The Headliners The live bill is built on contrast, and that is deliberate. 9ice legendary entertainer, bringing decades of Lagos street credibility into a room full of emerging talent. This is a statement about continuity: the old guard is standing next to the new one. Fido is a performance you don’t want to miss, because you know Joy is coming! For a night that asks the crowd to care who wins, a distinctly local identity is a useful anchor. JAYBERRY brings vibrant energy with heartfelt lyrics. That pairing is harder than it sounds. Energy without substance is cho cho cho; substance without energy is a let down. Access is tiered, and the structure is worth understanding before you buy. All tickets available here . VS: General admission: ₦20,000 (about $16 on an international card). VSOP table, seats 4 XO table, seats 7 The tiers are named for the drinks poured on the night, which suits a Hennessy-backed event. The tables are clearly built for groups who want a base for the night, not just a spot at the rail. Why It Matters Beyond One Night Green Indie describes itself as Africa’s first Direct-to-Fan music platform, selling music directly to listeners rather than routing it through labels. Indie Star Search is the most visible expression of that philosophy: it hands part of the discovery decision to the audience. Whether or not you buy the platform’s broader claims, the event tests an idea. In a creative economy where algorithms often decide what gets heard, a room that votes in real time offers a different signal. It is messier, louder, and more human. item.title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Faces Crucial Test As 100 Million Voters Await 2027 Elections
item.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. It comes against the backdrop of lingering controversies surrounding the 2023 general elections, particularly the failure to upload presidential election results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) in real time, technical difficulties associated with BVAS and allegations of electoral irregularities. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. The commission’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Meci, explained that the exercise would allow INEC to establish the effectiveness and reliability of its equipment before election day. “We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. Amupitan disclosed on Wednesday, during a meeting with resident electoral commissioners from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, that the clean-up followed the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System and a statutory claims-and-objections audit. item.title: UK privacy watchdog faces probe into its workplace culture
item.description: Britain's privacy watchdog is getting a taste of its own medicine, with an independent review set to examine the culture, governance, and accountability surrounding the events that led to former Information Commissioner John Edwards' resignation. Karon Monaghan KC will examine whether the regulator's culture and governance allowed problems to develop or made concerns harder to raise. Edwards quit in June after an independent workplace investigation found there was a "case to answer" over his behavior and that his conduct fell short of what was expected of a public official. He disagreed with some of its findings, but ultimately conceded that he had shown "poor judgment." That investigation, however, focused on Edwards alone. According to the terms of reference published on Thursday, it "did not consider the wider conditions in which that conduct occurred, and it was not designed to." The new review will cast a wider net. Monaghan wants to know whether staff could call out bad behavior further up the food chain, and what awaited those who tried. It will also poke around the regulator's leadership and governance arrangements and its relationship with its sponsoring government department, including whether there were adequate ways for concerns to be escalated and those at the top to be challenged. Current and former staff can give evidence confidentially and voluntarily, while Monaghan will be given access to relevant documents and existing material, including staff surveys and data on bullying, harassment and discrimination. The ICO has confirmed it won't use confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements to prevent people from contributing to the review. Monaghan decides which witnesses and documents are relevant, rather than the ICO or DCMS. Access remains subject to legal restrictions, and she must be told when material is withheld and why. She can speak to whoever she thinks is relevant and ask for the complaints, correspondence, and other paperwork she needs. And if that leads her somewhere unexpected, she can ask to widen the investigation. DCMS can refuse, but it won't be able to quietly brush the request aside, and any decision not to expand the scope has to make it into the final report. The review won't reopen the investigation into Edwards, make findings about the conduct of named individuals, or delve into the merits of the regulator's enforcement decisions. Its arrival comes amid a broader shake-up at Britain's data watchdog. The old Information Commissioner's Office was formally replaced by the Information Commission on September 30, bringing with it a new board-led governance model. The government first promised the wider review in July, shortly after Edwards' departure, but it didn't appoint its reviewer or nail down the terms until late November. item.title: JJ Abrams’ Sci-Fi Thriller Found-Footage Masterpiece Is Being Removed From Paramount Plus
item.description: In some ways, the best found-footage movie ever made is still The Blair Witch Project . This wasn’t because of the film’s actual quality, but because of the effect it had on audiences back in 1999. When it was released, found-footage movies just weren't a well-known thing and the marketing campaign for the movie made it seem as though the events depicted actually happened. Since then, better found-footage movies have been made that have replay value — a quality The Blair Witch Project sorely lacks — but none since have ever tricked audiences quite so effectively.

item.title: Rocket Lab sending Japanese satellite to orbit on Thanksgiving Day launch: Watch it live
item.description: null Rocket Lab will add another satellite to a growing Japanese Earth-observation constellation today (Nov. 26), and you can watch the action live. An Electron rocket carrying a radar imaging satellite for Tokyo-based Earth-observation company Synspective is scheduled to lift off from Rocket Lab 's New Zealand launch site today, during a window that opens at 7:00 p.m. ET (0000 GMT and 1:00 p.m. on Nov. 27 in New Zealand). You can watch the mission, called "Night Owls Never Sleep," via Rocket Lab starting about 30 minutes before liftoff. Space.com will carry the company's stream if, as expected, it's made available. Synspective is building a network of "Strix" spacecraft equipped with synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which uses radio waves to generate detailed images of Earth's surface in both day and night lighting, as well as through cloud cover. Today's launch will be Rocket Lab's 14th for Synspective to date, and there are a lot more coming. At the end of September, Rocket Lab announced a deal with the company for an additional 20 Electron missions between 2028 and 2031 — the largest commercial launch contract in the rocket's history. That agreement brought Synspective's total number of contracted Electron flights to 47. Synspective aims to eventually establish a constellation capable of imaging locations anywhere on Earth at intervals of just a few hours. The patch for Rocket Lab's "Night Owls Never Sleep" mission. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) If all goes to plan today, the Electron's kick stage will deploy the Strix satellite into low Earth orbit , 569 kilometers (353.6 miles) above our planet. "Night Owl Never Sleeps" will be the 101st mission to date for Rocket Lab. Ninety-two of them have been orbital flights with Electron; the other nine have been missions with HASTE , a suborbital variant of Electron that allows customers to test sensors and other equipment in the hypersonic flight environment.

item.title: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally The 2019 Lightning conference in Berlin was lit: five hundred “cypherpunks” getting each other high on visions of a future with peer-to-peer electronic cash. Attending a bitcoin conference back in the day felt like being a teenager at a friend’s party while their parents were out of town. It was exciting and new. The feeling was the opposite of FOMO: something big was happening, we were on the inside, and the rest of the world was going to envy us. It was the kind of party that you could only have when the adults weren’t looking. Whenever someone bought a beer (with bitcoin), everyone would hoot and holler and record it on their phones for Instagram/Twitter (it was still called Twitter). Lightning was the bleeding edge. We called it “the Lightning Network” (capitalized, if you please), and talking about it felt like talking about string theory: something so far out you’re not even sure it’s real. I spent a lot of time invoking the abacus . Those are the times some of us remember fondly and keep trying to relive at bitcoin conferences today. That’s why we engage in rituals like drone shows, Satoshi Rockamoto sets, beefsteak dinners , and video game tournaments for sats, but it’s not the same. The ratio of bitcoin OG speakers to suits is shifting. Many event rooms are half empty, and the halls and meeting rooms are full of people negotiating cap tables and profit-sharing splits. The adults haven’t shut the party down, but they have crashed it, and it kinda feels like their party now. The most exciting thing I noticed at the last bitcoin conference I attended was that nothing exciting happened. And that’s worth celebrating. From Tech Subcultures to Mainstream Tech Adoption The road to boring is seldom smooth. Technological innovation benefits from passion and bold ideas. People work harder on a project when they feel strongly about it and identify closely with like-minded collaborators. That’s where tech subcultures, their rituals, and their dogmas come from. But such passion and tribalism feed conflict, at least for a while until the tech goes mainstream, and normies, who couldn’t care less about subculture squabbles, take over. This progression from an exciting new technology that inspires strong emotions to a humdrum utility is not unusual. World-changing innovations often (always?) start with a committed subculture that identifies fiercely with their weird tech before the mainstream adopts it and soon expects it. In fact, this trajectory has become the standard doctrine of tech marketing. For example, in the early days of the internet, early adopters wrote a Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace , picking a fight with states and corporations despite having nothing to back it up but chatrooms and dreams. One case that resembles the early days of bitcoin was the war of the currents between high-voltage AC current and low-voltage DC current in the 1880s-1890s. Both featured big personaliti

item.title: 'Significant number of customer records' pwned in Flight Centre Travel Group breach
item.description: Travel giant Flight Centre Travel Group (FLT) says "a significant number of customer records" may have been accessed by "unknown persons" following a cyberattack. The Brisbane-headquartered company said the incident affected a third-party accommodation booking system used by Flight Centre, Travel Associates, Cruiseabout, and some independent travel agents. Its disclosure [PDF], filed with the Australian Securities Exchange today, added that it was aware that records were accessed, but cannot definitively say how many were exfiltrated. Flight Centre is working with the supplier and incident response specialist Mandiant to establish the scope of the incident. An initial review suggests most accessed records contained only customer names, some with basic travel information. A "very small percentage" may also include birth dates, email addresses, limited passport details, phone numbers, or, in rare cases, health or mobility information. Flight bookings and corporate travel use separate systems and are unaffected, the company said. "FLT values customer privacy and data security," the company said in its disclosure. "The company understands that an incident like this can be unsettling for customers who may be affected, and we apologize for any concern this causes." Investigations remain ongoing, but FLT has already contained the attack, rotated keys and credentials, and increased system monitoring, it said. The company said it would contact affected customers directly. Its brands continue to operate normally, and travelers should proceed with their plans. Customers should independently verify unexpected messages about their bookings before clicking links, opening attachments, or sharing personal information. The attack on FLT follows others that have hit booking systems in the past year, including those on Booking.com and BWH Hotels . More recently, another Australian business, RMS Cloud, which provides booking software to travel and leisure companies, also acknowledged a breach that led to WhatsApp scams in late October. Numerous reports of travelers being targeted with messages that contained their names and booking details hit local news outlets at the time. Customers were sent convincing messages seemingly from the hotels they had booked, and according to Australia's National Anti-Scam Centre, the scams appeared to be financially motivated. Muhammad Yahya Patel, vCISO and cybersecurity advisor for EMEA at Huntress, said attackers targeting booking systems is a "familiar supply chain story" that has a greater impact than simple data theft. Speaking generally about the risks of exposed travel records, Patel said: "Unlike a compromised email address or phone number, a passport can't be changed easily or quickly. For affected customers, the practical risk extends well beyond the immediate breach. item.title: Driver Arrested Over Crash, Inferno That Killed 31 In Egypt
item.description: Egyptian prosecutors announced on Thursday the arrest of a man accused of causing a massive fire that erupted when a fuel tanker overturned on a packed highway in Cairo, killing 31 people. The prosecution said the man had “admitted” to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, “causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course”. When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added. This video grab taken from UGC images posted on social media on November 25, 2026, shows flames engulfing the area during a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Footage from the scene showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital’s Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists on the ring road sounded their horns and struggled to get away.The prosecution said an investigation is underway to determine the driver’s criminal liability.The health ministry put the final toll at 31 dead and 21 wounded.More than 20 million people live in Greater Cairo, a sprawling and dense metropolis. With its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years. Car crashes are common and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance, and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency. Flames And Smoke In 2018, the government issued a decision banning heavy transport vehicles from accessing the ring road around Greater Cairo from 6:00 am to midnight. Emergency services personnel and bystanders gather beside the wreckage of a tanker truck following a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate, on November 25, 2026. Photo by MAHMOUD EL-KHAWAS / AFP Wednesday’s disaster occurred at around 7:00 pm — at a time when the road was packed with pedestrians, buses and cars.Traffic had returned to normal in the early hours of Thursday after rescue operations ended and the wreckage of the truck and burned-out cars was cleared.”We were driving on the flyover above the ring road and saw flames rising to a height I can’t even describe,” said Wagih Ragheb, a witness to the disaster.”Then the explosions started… We got out of the car and went down to the ring road and found a catastrophic situation: buses and cars completely charred, and many dead.” Footage posted online by passersby showed people pulling others out of their cars in the inferno that erupted after the truck overturned. “We have a problem with our roads. These accidents happen very often, and no one knows how to solve this,” said Abdel Rahman Ahmed, who was at a Cairo hospital to donate blood for the wounded. item.title: Cosmic 'betta fish' glows in spectacular nebula portrait | Space photo of the day for Nov. 26, 2026
item.description: null An image captured by the Dark Energy Camera showcasing the Betta Fish Nebula. (Image credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA) The striking blue of the Betta Fish Nebula swims across the cosmic landscape, a stunning wisp of material leftover from a stellar explosion. What is it? Roughly 6,800 light-years from Earth and nestled in the Centaurus constellation, this piece of the supernova remnant SNR G295.5+09.7 has earned the nickname the Betta Fish Nebula for its floaty, fishy shape. This almost ghostly whirl of gas and dust was created when a star much more massive than our sun exploded, blasting its outer layers of material outward in the process. Over time, the remnants of this supernova eruption stretched outward into space, dispersing and colliding with surrounding gas. The explosive remnants mixing with gas in the interstellar medium created this glowing, blue cloud. This celestial scene was captured by the Dark Energy Camera (DECam), that was created by the U.S. Department of Energy. The camera is installed on the National Science Foundation's Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile. Why is it incredible? This image of a colossal, cosmic "fish" was captured by a camera meant to study the illusive effects of dark energy , which is the name scientists have given for whatever mysterious something is causing the universe to expand at an accelerating rate . The camera is used as part of the Dark Energy Survey, a six-year, international collaboration in which scientists have collected observations of hundreds of millions of galaxies, thousands of supernova and additional details about our cosmos that could help to fill in the picture of the nature of dark energy. And while researchers this past January revealed the initial result of this six-year survey, scientists continue to explore the possibilities of dark energy with DECam alongside instruments like the recently-launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. However, while the survey has lofty goals with its DECam data, the camera can also capture beautiful imagery like this cerulean wisp thousands of light-years away.

item.title: Rackspace pulls plug on Spot cloud service after security breach
item.description: Rackspace is shutting down its low-cost Spot cloud service after a security breach, giving customers two weeks' notice to move their workloads and retrieve their data. In a notice posted on Tuesday , the cloud computing biz said its Rackspace Spot service will cease operations at 1700 Central Time (2300 UTC) on December 8. Any workloads still running at that point will be terminated, and customers will no longer be able to access their data. "Following the recent security incident affecting Rackspace Spot, Rackspace has made the decision to wind down the service," the company said. "Spot customers are being notified with the wind-down timeline, instructions for retrieving their data and steps to secure their environments." Customers will have to contend with the fallout from the breach while simultaneously trying to get their applications and data off the platform. According to a customer notification seen by The Register , the attackers used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot over a period of almost 22 hours on November 17. Rackspace only learned of the intrusion the following day, after a customer raised the alarm. The intruders impersonated legitimate users, created pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, gained access to stored credentials known as Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and storage volumes. "With that access, they could have read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held," Rackspace told customers. Rackspace has since revoked the affected tokens and sessions, removed the pods planted by the intruders, and changed the affected platform and storage keys. Customers must also reissue API tokens, download new Kubernetes configuration files, and rotate credentials stored in their clusters, including database passwords and third-party API keys. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and chief growth officer of Platform9, which co-developed Spot with Rackspace, shed some light on the root cause in a November 20 GitHub post. "An observability system was breached using a compromised credential," Raghuram wrote. "This was obviously a critical error on our part and we are very sorry we let this happen." Raghuram said the incident necessitated significant changes to the underlying infrastructure clusters, prolonging the outage. Spot's selling point was cheap compute. The service operated an auction-based pricing model, allowing customers to bid for cloud infrastructure at a fraction of the cost of conventional on-demand instances. Rackspace advertised savings of up to 90 percent for customers willing to tolerate interruptions to their workloads. A permanent interruption probably wasn't what they had in mind. Rackspace hasn't explained why it chose closure over recovery, revealed how many customers were affected, or said whether it will offer migration extensions. It did not respond to The Register's questions. ®

item.title: Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack
item.description: Peninsula Energy has temporarily shut down its Wyoming uranium operation after a "cybersecurity incident" affected plant and wellfield control systems. The Australian uranium producer said on Wednesday that it had activated its response procedures and brought in outside specialists following the attack on its US subsidiary, Strata Energy, which operates the Lance uranium project. Peninsula Energy said it believes the attack is "confined to the plant and wellfield operating and control systems," and that back-office functions, such as payroll and other corporate systems, in both the US and Australia, remain unaffected. "The company's immediate priorities have been to protect the safety of its employees, secure its operating systems, and work towards the restoration of operations in a safe and controlled manner," it said in an update to the Australian Securities Exchange. The notification [PDF] went on to say that Peninsula Energy's investigations into the attack, including whether any data was compromised, remain ongoing. Peninsula has not given a restart date and says it cannot yet assess the impact on its 2027 production guidance. Operations will remain suspended until recovery and safety checks are complete. "Peninsula will provide further updates to the market as material information becomes available," it said. The disclosure of additional information came two days after Peninsula secured a short trading halt, which referenced a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming site. The November 23 filing [PDF] dated the incident to Friday evening in Western Australia. Wednesday's update clarified that Strata detected it on the morning of November 20, local US time. Peninsula subsequently requested a voluntary suspension of trading until the earlier of November 30 or an announcement on restarting operations and any resulting change to production guidance. Peninsula's Lance project is a uranium mining operation, extracting the element from underground deposits and turning it into uranium concentrate, aka yellowcake or U₃O₈. Uranium concentrate is feedstock for nuclear fuel production, typically undergoing conversion, enrichment, and fabrication into uranium dioxide pellets before use in reactors. The Lance central processing plant was constructed to produce a maximum of 2.0 million pounds (Mlb) of U₃O₈ annually, and is licensed for 3.0 Mlb. Peninsula previously forecast production of 500,000 to 600,000 pounds in 2027, having withdrawn its 2026 guidance earlier this year following operational problems at Lance. It now says it will reassess the 2027 outlook once operations resume. ®
